text:
This came in to me in a box within a box. Basically expected packaging. If you got your drive in any other form of packaging as reported by other users, you probably bought the drive from a different retailer. My order was fulfilled by Amazon. If it says it's being sold by another retailer, I wouldn't trust it. Even if their reputation is good. (Unless it's a retailer I know and trust)

I ran some benchmarks using Crystal Disk Mark, and here are my results.
Seagate drive NEW MODEL (The one shown here)
Read: 195.1 MB/s
Write: 192.6 MB/s

Sandisk Z400m m.2 SSD
Read: 558.5 MB/s
Write: 187.3 MB/s

Seagate drive OLD MODEL (32% Capacity Full)
Read: 175.2 MB/s
Write 138.2 MB/s
In case most of you don't know, when a HDD reaches over 40% capacity, it starts to slow down dramatically. My old drive is 32% full so it's slightly slower than it should be.

I'll be using this as a dedicated media storage and recording drive, and these results are very much what I need. I run Windows 10 and other programs on my SSD, my games are dedicated to my old Seagate drive, and now my media and video recordings will be dedicated to this new drive.
If you're looking to buy this drive to run your Windows/Linux OS, then look towards getting and SSD for that instead, and using a seperate drive for games/media. If you can't afford the combo, see if you can get Seagates FireCuda line-up. It's built to have responsive Windows load times and keep the capacity of a normal HDD.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'm using the 5TB version of this drive to host all my movie files. I've owned these drives for about 7 months now, and went across the world with these in my carry on. It works great and I haven't had any issues yet. I'm using this on a 5k maxed out iMac with the Plex Media Server to stream content to any device on my home or remote networks. All I did was reformat this drive to Mac's Journaled formatting (via Disk Utility) and didn't want to install the NTFS driver as I'm all Apple here. I bought two drives and use one that is connected 24x7 to my Mac and use the other as a back up locked up in a fire proof safe when not in use. I've also turned off the "Put Hard Drives to Sleep" function so that it is always spinning (plex has an issue with sleeping hard drives). Transfer rates are good. I've transferred about 1700 movie files (over 2TBs of data) in about 5 hours going from my the 1st 5TB drive to the 2nd 5TB drive (completely blank) over USB 3. The only time transfer speeds suffer is when doing lots of deletes and transfers simultaneously (for example, swapping out a standard definition movie for a higher definition movie). For smaller transfers, it's quick. I can transfer a 2GB movie from my Apple's SSD to this in under 1 minute. When transferring lots of data, I have both hooked up to my computer's UPS just in case of power failure (which is common here in Korea).

The footprint and texture of the drives are nice. I just have them standing on my desk and they take up little real estate. There is a slight hum that comes from the hard drive, which isn't too distracting. It uses a USB 3 cable and a separate power cable. There is a blue light that blinks at a constant rate when transferring data. It will be solid if the drive is on, but nothing is reading or writing. It turns off after about 5 minutes of no activity which you can disable in your computer's power saver settings. It takes about 10 to 15 seconds to spin up.

I'm looking at purchasing two more drives as I'm running out of room, and might go for the 8TB of this same model to store my movies, and use the 5TBs to store all my seasons and shows.

Remember to always have a back up strategy as these drives can fail without warning. Also, ensure you eject the drive from your computer (click the eject button in OS X's finder window) and let the drive spin down before moving.

Overall, I would recommend these drives to anyone who needs to archive lots of data.

- running in raid 5 using Microsoft spaces, I'm getting incredible download speeds from the drives. Mind you one by itself is really slow, but 60!? Runs sooooo fast.
- Relatively efficiently cool. I have these things stacked in 4 rows of 15 drives. Hard disk sentinal reads relative disk temps between 30-38 degrees. There's 8 fans in a push and pull configuration (2 per row) for active cooling, but still there's a lot of hard drives in a rather confined space, temps are great.
- Low noise. With so many drives running I expected a bunch of noise. They are really quiet. Even when I was transferring 45tb of storage over my 10gbps network onto the system I couldn't hear anything but the case fans.
- ZERO failures. Like literally zero. I haven't killed one yet. I've got 4 spare drives just waiting to swap out a dead drive but it hasn't happened yet. The lack of failures is amazing.

As both a gamer and someone who values functional collectibles, the Seagate Starfield Special Edition Game Drive hits the sweet spot between performance and aesthetics. Performance
For an HDD, this drive is impressively responsive. I tested it for:

Extra Value – 3-Year Rescue Services

The Seagate Starfield Special Edition Game Drive 2TB is perfect for gamers who want reliable performance, ample storage, and a design that stands out. It’s not just an external hard drive—it’s a display piece that enhances your gaming setup while giving you the storage you need.

text: I bought the 6TB version to upgrade my PLEX server. Based on other reviews I immediately checked the warranty. Just search for "Seagate Drive Warranty" in your search engine and enter the serial number. Mine checked out with warranty valid for 2 years and 1 month. If you are installing a drive larger than 2TB (in windows), you must use GPT disk partitioning instead of MBR to recognize the full size of the disk. MBR is an older partition style used in legacy bios'. You must switch to the newer UEFI bios and then convert the disk to GPT partition using the windows disk management system. (I'm not sure about iOS). Since W10 v1703 you can convert to UEFI without reinstalling. Just search for "switch to uefi without reinstall" and follow the instructions. It only took me 10 minutes to switch to UEFI, then partition the disk as GPT instead of MBR. Full drive size recognized and running great so far.

This Is a 3.5 drive, so be sure that it will fit your console or whatever you are placing it in. It's important that people know this is not a standard drive and is made for surveillance cameras, or something that is access to an overridden on a regular basis. Unlike a standard hard drive in your PC that has correction control most of these drives for the surveillance systems do not have correction. Meaning once it copies the data there is no verification that the data was copied correctly. Why this is not usually a problem on a system is a good hard drive and a smooth running operating system it could result in data loss. That is why it is advised to buy a surveillance hard drive, something that is specifically made to run off and and to keep copying the files without correction.

I found a hard drive to be very efficient, and for some reason works faster than my 1 TB of the same maker and brand. It is also quieter than the 1 TB that my system came with. In fact the fan on my DVR makes more noise than a hard drive does and I have a quiet fan.

Keep in mind why this may fit the majority of DVR's that are out there formats do vary from Linux, Windows or their own proprietary software. And formatting the drive may vary. Generally speaking most surveillance hard drives are compatible with buried systems but keep in mind that your hard drive may need to be formatted either by the DVR system, or possibly externally done to make it compatible with your DVR. I have seen more people have problems with DVR hard drives when they do not realize that the system they are installing in a have a proprietary format system and may not be compatible with the drive you purchased. That is why it's important to find a hard drive that has a wide range of compatibility as well is something that's been around for a while. Your surveillance cameras are expensive investment for most people. And the data that we have on these hard drives is why they are valuable. Anybody can purchase DVR, and cameras are pretty similar across the board improving with each year. But hard drives are the core operating systems bread-and-butter of you will. When you need the hard drive to work you need to work, this is barely second two cameras being of high quality because you have a high-quality camera but if your hard drive is a standard drive or of a low quality you may have issues. So if you've invested the camera system it's wise to buy a compatible high-quality hard drive that is built for surveillance systems and has a decent warranty.

text:
After using the Seagate Expansion 6TB Desktop Drive for well over a year, it’s become a core part of my home office setup. If you're looking for a large, reliable external drive without the bells and whistles, this one gets the job done.

Setup is as simple as it gets—plug it into the power source and connect it via USB 3.0, and it's ready to go. There’s no complicated software to install or setup wizards to fight with. I've used it primarily for backups, media libraries, and some game storage, and it handles all of it with ease. Transfer speeds are respectable for an HDD; I average around 120–150 MB/s, which is more than enough for moving big video files or system images.

The build is sturdy enough for a desktop drive. It’s not meant to be portable, and at over a kilogram in weight, it should stay on a desk. That said, the textured casing resists fingerprints and looks clean, even after long-term use. Just be aware that it does require external power, which adds one more plug to your setup.

The real selling point is reliability. Over a year in, with regular use, I haven’t run into a single issue—no disconnections, no overheating, no corrupted files. Seagate also includes a 3-year Rescue Data Recovery plan, which is reassuring even though I haven’t needed it.

If you're a creative professional, media hoarder, or just want peace of mind with your backups, the Seagate Expansion 6TB is a solid, no-fuss option. It's not flashy, it's not fast like an SSD—but it works every single time, and that's exactly what I wanted.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the 16TB unit with front USB hub to store photographs and some miscellaneous files. My unit is connected to a dual-boot (Windows 10 & Ubuntu) laptop workstation through a USB hub.

After I connected the USB cable, I plugged in the drive's power cord and Seagate One Touch Hub fired right up. I moved 50,000 files, totaling about 500GB to the drive to confirm that everything was working, and then fired up Lightroom and had it 'add' a year's worth of pictures to it's catalog. Everything worked fine. I then booted up Ubuntu to confirm that Ubuntu could see and access the disk, and it did so without any issues.

While I did not benchmark the unit, it's speed seemed typical of other hard drives. That is, while much slower than a SSD, is plenty fast enough for photo storage.

The unit has only a very small disk activity LED on the front of the unit. There are no other lights on the unit. When you first add the unit to a Windows system, the drive will appear in the 'Desktop' view of the File Manager. Normally File Manager defaults to showing you the 'Quick Access' - Frequent Folders and Recent Files view.

The unit isn't silent - no hard disk drive is - and it does make sounds when it's spinning the disk platters up to speed after 'sleeping' and when the disk is moving the disk heads to read or write a file. The rest of the time the unit is essentially silent. It's safe to say that this disk is nosier than any disk I've had before (it's also a LOT bigger than any disk I've had before), but the sounds this unit makes are no louder than everyday background office noises. Personally, I don't find them objectionable.

I am pleased with the 16TB Seagate One Touch Hub I purchased. The unit is performing like I expected it to, and I expect it will serve me well for a number of years.

Estoy muy contento con el Seagate One Touch Hub de 8 TB. Este disco duro externo es perfecto para mis necesidades de almacenamiento, especialmente para mi trabajo con videos en 4K.
Con 8 TB de espacio, puedo guardar todos mis videos, fotos y documentos sin preocuparme por el espacio. Es ideal para manejar grandes cantidades de datos.

Velocidad Rápida
Gracias a su conexión USB-C y USB 3.0, las transferencias de archivos son rápidas. Mover archivos grandes, como videos en 4K, es mucho más rápido y sencillo.

Funcionalidad de HUB
Lo mejor de este modelo es que puedo conectar mi móvil o portátil directamente al disco duro. Esto facilita cargar dispositivos y transferir archivos sin complicaciones, porque para los videos de YouTube grabo muchos recursos con el IPhone y Time-lapses con otro smartphone, y pasar todos los archivos por telegram era muchísimo tiempo.

El diseño es elegante y funciona bien con ordenadores de sobremesa, portátiles y Mac. Es compacto y no ocupa mucho espacio.

Refrigeración y Ruido
El disco duro prácticamente ni se escucha, y demás refrigera bastante bien, analizándolo con CrystalDisk mientras paso 300GB de video no pasa de 42ºC y estamos en Mayo, con unos 22ºC en mi estudio.

Conclusión
El Seagate One Touch Hub de 8 TB es una excelente inversión. Su gran capacidad, rapidez y funcionalidad adicional lo hacen destacar. ¡Muy recomendado!

Il NAS Synology 223j è davvero un prodotto eccellente, all’altezza della fama del marchio. Sin dall’apertura della confezione, si percepisce la qualità costruttiva: un design compatto e discreto, perfetto per ogni ambiente, che non occupa troppo spazio ma offre grandi prestazioni. 🏠

La configurazione è stata semplice e veloce, anche per chi non ha molta esperienza con i NAS. L’interfaccia DiskStation Manager (DSM) è come sempre intuitiva, ben organizzata e ricca di funzionalità. 💡 Nonostante sia un modello base, è più che sufficiente per l’uso domestico o per un piccolo ufficio. L’archiviazione e la gestione dei file sono incredibilmente fluide, permettendo di organizzare tutto in modo efficiente. 🗂️

Un altro punto di forza è la gestione impeccabile dei backup: la possibilità di creare copie di sicurezza dei dati è essenziale, e con il Synology 223j tutto avviene in maniera automatica e sicura. 🔒 Inoltre, la sincronizzazione dei file su più dispositivi è rapida e senza intoppi, rendendo facile accedere ai dati ovunque ci si trovi. 📱💻

Nonostante il prezzo contenuto rispetto a modelli più avanzati, questo NAS offre una versatilità impressionante: streaming di contenuti multimediali, accesso remoto, protezione RAID dei dati... praticamente tutto ciò di cui si ha bisogno! 🎥📂

In sintesi, se cercate un NAS affidabile, facile da usare e con le caratteristiche essenziali per proteggere e gestire i vostri dati, il Synology 223j è la scelta giusta. 🔝 Un investimento che non deluderà, come da tradizione del brand! 🌟

text:
The DS223 is an excellent choice for hosting your own private cloud. The DS223 is the first ARM based NAS to natively support Docker. This NAS can easily run a few docker containers without any issues. I run this NAS with two Seagate Exos x18 18TB drives in RAID 1.

However, don’t expect this NAS to do compute tasks very well. Unpacking a rar file takes much longer on this NAS compared to my intel g4560t server (which is a hyperthreaded dual core CPU). However, it does this task without maxing the CPU which is a good thing. I also would not recommend this NAS if you are planning to run mediaservers such as Plex or Emby. In that case I’d recommend running a small server alongside it such as HP ProDesk or Lenovo Thinkcentre which usually has more powerful hardware compared to the DS224+.

The only downside this NAS has compared to the DS224+ is the lack of an extra gigabit port and lack of RAM expansion.

Overall I think this NAS is a great choice.

text: J'ai acheté ce petit serveur NAS pour sauvegarder des fichiers pro et personnels. Jusqu'à présent, j'ai toujours utilisé des disques durs externes pour cette tâche et je me disais qu'un Nas c'était trop compliqué à installer, à configurer... Sur les conseils d'un ami, j'ai acheté ce boîtier et je dois dire que je ne suis pas déçu. L'installation du disque dur (un Seagate Ironwolf acheté séparément) était vraiment très facile: on ouvre le panneau frontal clipsé, on sort un tiroir, on retire deux petits clips que l'on replace juste ensuite pour tenir le disque dur, on réinsére le tiroir et c'est fini. Une fois branché sur sa box, on se connecte au NAS via une adresse web ou un QR code pour mobile et il n'y a qu'à suivre les instructions d'installation. En quelques minutes, on peut profiter de son cloud privé. C'est vraiment très accessible pour tout le monde. Sinon rien à redire sur le fonctionnement. Pour ma part, je pense qu'il est très silencieux. Le ventilateur se met en route très occasionnellement comme sur n'importe quel ordinateur mais la plupart du temps on ne l'entend pas du tout. La suite logicielle est un peu moins intuitive que l'installation, il faut se familiariser mais rien de très compliqué non plus. A noter qu'il y a déjà un petit câble réseau fourni dans la boîte (1m environ), personne ne le mentionne, j'en avais acheté un supplémentaire inutilement. Le boîtier est compact, élégant et léger. Je recommanderais ce NAS aux néophytes sans hésiter.

It took me longer working with Amazon to get a solid answer as to who specifically sold this to me through the Amazon refurb store than it did for RenewByte to solve my problem. All you need in this case is the right Product key and you can upgrade Home to Pro in-place (in case you didn't know that).

RenewByte was ON IT. As soon as I figured out it was them (and not the three other places Amazon pointed me at) they listened to the problem, understood the problem as I articulated it, and got me the right product key, which, of course, worked. My wife's system now has Win 11 Pro, not Home and all it took was a reboot to complete the process once I put the key in.

They could have, and I indeed have had other refurb groups run me around the mulberry bush to do a return because that's somehow "easier" for them when the only problem is something small like a card failed that I could replace on my own. THANK YOU, RenewByte, I will be looking to you for my future needs in this class of machine without looking at others, based on your customer service.

Great machine, but two cons that might leave some people stuck and disappointed.
First the potential biggy. The system came with NO power cord. Oops!
Also, as other another review stated, the Wi-Fi is NOT built in by DELL as the description states. It is a tiny $5 USB type
but it works just fine and this makes no difference to me, but it might to some.
FYI, if you get this machine and the Wi-Fi sees access points but will not connect, try a different USB port. I started with the 4th USB3 (blue) port on the right and no go. I moved it to the first on the left, and it has been solid now for a few days. I don't know why this would happen, but I got it working so no big deal.
Neither of those issues flustered me, your mileage may vary.
I got this refurb PC because of its 8 core i7-9700, 32GB RAM and 1TB SDD all for a great price.

The build quality and the heavy sheet metal used in these units is far superior to a discount consumer grade PC. I have had four similar mini towers like this over the years - 2 HP and 2 DELL, but this is the most powerful one yet. The $400 price point makes it a no-brainer for most business and home office uses. It runs Win11, Libre Office, some trading and charting platforms, and FL Studio DAW all at the same time without hesitation. The 32GB RAM no doubt helps with that.
The unit arrived well packed for shipping and reasonably clean, though it had what I thought at first was a small scratch on top. This turned out to be a splash of white-out from its past corporate life.
As I mentioned above, what could be a showstopper for most users looking for a turnkey machine, this unit arrived with no power cord. Now, having been a PC hardware nerd for decades, I have dozens of the standard power cords laying around, and it did not slow me down a bit. Obviously, though, a power cord should come in the box, and most likely will in yours. I can't imagine they left it out on purpose.
I have not tested the included CHEAP wireless keyboard and mouse, but I am sure they are fine for what they are and are probably an upgrade for laptop keyboard users.
Great value, in a small, solid package.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: It came with Windows and when I turned it on, it picked up wifi signals and would not let me skip this step. Another reason to run Linux. Opened it up, did a good job cleaning out the dust, underneath the fan, cIeaned it out more. I came with an Intel Wireless/Bluetooth m2 card. Removed and reset all memory, m2 devices. Boot LMDE6, UEFI install. Everything works.... until I disconnect power. It keeps losing the date and boot config everything the power is disconnected. And it turns on by itself when the power is reconnected. Replaced 2032 battery, reinstall linux, reset BIOS to factory defaults, flash updated BIOS (can be done from BIOS screen and USB drive), still losing BIOS settings on power disconnect. Searching online... Solution: remove motherboard jumper from JMP1 (pin 3-4), turn on, BIOS message will say password is reset, turn off, replace jumper and it's all fixed. Everything works.

THANK YOU, RenewByte, I will be looking to you for my future needs in this class of machine without looking at others, based on your customer service.

First the potential biggy. The system came with NO power cord. Oops!

I moved it to the first on the left, and it has been solid now for a few days. I don't know why this would happen, but I got it working so no big deal.
Neither of those issues flustered me, your mileage may vary.
I got this refurb PC because of its 8 core i7-9700, 32GB RAM and 1TB SDD all for a great price.

The unit arrived well packed for shipping and reasonably clean, though it had what I thought at first was a small scratch on top. This turned out to be a splash of white-out from its past corporate life.

Now, having been a PC hardware nerd for decades, I have dozens of the standard power cords laying around, and it did not slow me down a bit. Obviously, though, a power cord should come in the box, and most likely will in yours. I can't imagine they left it out on purpose.
I have not tested the included CHEAP wireless keyboard and mouse, but I am sure they are fine for what they are and are probably an upgrade for laptop keyboard users.
Great value, in a small, solid package.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The OptiPlex 7050 Micro turns out to be a surprisingly capable little lab box, especially when you throw Linux on it and let it breathe. The i7-6700T may be older, but paired with 32GB of RAM, it handles Docker stacks, lightweight VMs, home-lab services, and general experimentation without breaking a sweat. For a machine roughly the size of a sandwich, it’s shockingly stable under continuous workloads—something you notice when it’s been running for days without a hiccup or thermal complaint.

In practice, it makes an excellent “utility node” for the kind of mixed tasks labs tend to accumulate: small containers, automation tools, monitoring agents, or a handful of personal services. And yes—it even runs a Minecraft server just fine. The kids don’t care that the CPU launched during the Obama administration; they care that it doesn’t lag when someone decides to dump 12 stacks of TNT. The SSD and RAM make the whole setup feel modern, and Linux has no trouble with the hardware, meaning you spend your time deploying things—not troubleshooting drivers.

Limitations are predictable and manageable: no GPU means anything graphics-heavy is off the table, and CPU-bound workloads will eventually remind you this isn’t a workstation-class chip. But for a quiet, low-power lab machine that sits on a shelf and just handles whatever odd job you give it, the 7050 Micro punches well above its weight. It’s one of those “why didn’t we repurpose these sooner?” machines—cheap to source, easy to maintain, and perfect for homelab and testing environments.

Pros
• Handles Linux, Docker, and small services extremely well
• 32GB RAM = plenty of headroom for containers and light VMs
• Quiet, low power, and stable under long uptimes
• Great for kid-friendly game servers (Minecraft, Valheim Lite, etc.)
• Inexpensive and plentiful on the refurb market

Cons
• Skylake CPU will bottleneck heavy multi-container or CI workloads
• No dedicated GPU limits certain lab scenarios
• Limited storage expansion (one M.2 slot)
• Not suitable for large databases or high-throughput services

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
NOTE: When I ordered this PC on 12/4/2022 it came from Skytech USA.

PROS:
1. Excellent condition - looks brand new. Couldn't find any scratches or defects. No dust or dirt visible inside or out.
2. As you can see from the pics, all the specs matched what was advertised.
3. Comes with boxed, basic keyboard and 2-button corded mouse. Full-sized keys & layout with a numeric keypad in a smaller-than-standard frame (17x5"). Has a soft, non-'clicky' tactile feel, and is mostly quiet with a little bit of key rattle.
4. On initial power up, you start with the standard Windows 10 setup of picking your region, keyboard, etc, so it was a fresh Windows install. No issues with activation.
5. Time from Dell logo appearing on screen to Windows desktop is about 10 seconds. Not too bad!
6. Very quiet. Even up close I can barely hear the fan - tho I've only run PVR software on it so far.
7. No bloatware. The only installed non-standard software was VLC Media Player.
8. Tool-less hardware mounting provides easy access to memory slots, swapping out storage devices, etc.

CONS:
1. Would have preferred a single 8GB RAM module vs the 2x4GB config it came with that uses up both slots. If you want to expand the memory you'll have to discard one or more of the existing modules.
2. Question the SATA SSD. I realize the object is to cut costs to the max, but for under 24 bucks you could install a same-sized, more reputable-brand M.2 NVMe drive for better performance, and free up the lone drive bay to boot. Makes one wonder just how cheap (reliable?) the included KingFast SSD is.

OTHER:
1. Cannot be upgraded to Windows 11. This may be a pro or con pending your viewpoint.
2. No wi-fi dongle or card included. Only network/internet connection is via ethernet cable. Not a deal breaker - dongles are cheap if you need wi-fi.
3. Installing an external graphic card could be problematic, unless it's low-power, half-height, and VERY thin. There's less than an inch of space between the slot and the side of the power supply (see pic). Plus, the PC's power supply is only 180 watts.
4. There are rubber feet on both the bottom and along the left side, so you can stand it vertical like a tower if desired.
5. RAM and M.2 slots are under the drive bay.
6. SHOULD you want to install a 3.5 HDD, the only full-size drive bay is filled with a caddy holding the SATA SSD. The caddy snaps out, but you'll have purchase a separate 3.5 caddy for your HDD as there is no inherent way to mount anything directly into the bay. Everything requires some manner of snap-in caddy.

The cons you kind of expect with this kind of product, so overall I give it 5 stars. I would not use it for high-end gaming. Don't know of a powerful enough half-height graphic card that would fit in the slot, but for non graphic-intensive tasks and some older games, this should work very well. So far, very happy with the purchase.

text:
Background: We are blessed in our family to have someone who knows a lot about PCs, so we’re not overly intimidated by needing to replace things inside a PC or trouble shooting. Some of the other purchaser’s negative reviews on this machine were daunting to me though, but the price was so good for the specs, we decided to try it in spite of some of the bad reviews. We concurrently use PCs and Macs of varying ages and operating systems. This is the 2d refurbished machine we’ve ever purchased (the other refurbished PC was a $100 refurbished HP years ago from Overstock.com that’s still working great), but from the varying experiences reflected in the reviews, it may be a bit of a roll of the dice. I like that Amazon is behind this product.

Experience so far: It’s been almost two months of DAILY HEAVY USE on this PC, even creating 3D graphics using Blender, and so far this PC is working great. Very fast efficient start up. Tackles memory hog tasks such as 3D rendering with Blender software well (especially for the price of the PC). However it’s relatively early days, so I still have some doubts of longevity (mostly because of the other Amazon reviews).
So for what it’s worth, here’s my experience so far (from the reviews it appears there’s quite a bit of difference from person to person so read others reviews too). I’m writing the good and bad.
1) The PC arrived NOT well packaged for shipping, so I was dubious it wasn’t damaged. I felt the packing was so bad it disrespected the customer’s time because it seemed so likely the PC would be damaged simply because of poor packaging. For example, the exterior shipping box was damaged and the there was way too much room inside the shipping box for the PC tower to slip around. Luckily, somehow our PC survived the shipping, but the seller should fix this easy fix. Dear Seller: Please pack the PCs as if you had to use the PC yourself. Why go through all that work in refurbishing only to risk screwing it up in the shipping? -so even though the PC actually did work (hurray!), it worked in spite of the sloppy packaging, so I’d rate the packaging as needlessly carelessly bad. It also made me hope the restoration was done with more care and pride in workmanship than the packing was. Not a confidence/goodwill builder, sadly.
2). The PC arrived with a very basic keyboard that is 100% perfect for my needs (I use four computers side-by-side, so keyboard space is at a premium, so I actually love the keyboard, nice large clear letters on each key, easy to read and yet still efficiently space saving).
3) The PC arrived with a basic mouse, a bit smaller-sized but works 100% fine.
4) The PC itself looks as it should, except the seller put a BIG ugly white service sticker on top of the PC in a prominent place, not at all attractive, so I hope the seller reads this and uses more discreet sticker placement for other buyers. The ugly large white service sticker essentially kills any aesthetic/freshness the PC Tower could have.
5) The PC came with a small white wireless dongle that if you want wireless will take up one of the USB ports.
6) With great intrepidation, fearing the worst due to the poor shipping packaging, I hooked up the PC to its mouse and keyboard (and one of my monitors) and turned on the PC. EVERYTHING worked fine. The wireless dongle worked. It booted up. It was super SUPER fast. Eventually we used Ethernet cable instead of wireless Wi-Fi, and the Ethernet connection works fine too. I’ve used the PC to read CDs/DVDs and burned a test DVD just to make sure it works. It does. At least so far :)
7) Because this PC is NOT upgradable to Win 11, etc., be realistic. AFTER I felt the PC was working by running it through its paces, that’s when I bought software for it. In other words, given the negative reviews, make sure you like what you get before investing in software, BUT BEFORE YOU BUY RESEARCH THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SOFTWARE YOU USE FOR WINDOWS 10 Pro. Once you’ve run the PC through its paces, that’s when I recommend you actually buy the most recent version of the software you use that is compatible with Windows 10pro, because eventually the software companies won’t be supporting Windows 10 anymore. (By way of example, the last version of Adobe Photoshop that you could buy to own (as opposed to rent monthly) is not compatible with operating systems past Windows 7, so for the rest of my life I’ll need a Windows 7 machine to use that older Adobe software; similarly if you don’t want to pay a monthly subscription fee for Word/Excel/etc., you’ll need to buy a version of Office that is still compatible with Windows 10 pro (I bought Office 2019 Pro).
8) So this PC has worked well for me with Blender, Outlook, Excel, Word, and the operating system/computer surprisingly came pre-loaded with various software things - even an interesting 3D program (that was a happy surprise, must be part of Windows 10 pro!?!), and I’ve used the PC for the internet, and the PC networked easily to the printer, etc.
9) Eventually all PCs die/fritz. I backup at least daily to an external hard drive, because you just never know (and this is a refurbished PC, especially given the reviews, be realistic and backup backup backup.
Bottom line: This is a speedy effective PC that so far is doing what I need it to do at a great price. There are some super easy fixes the seller can do (BETTER PACKAGING FOR SHIPPING & PLACE THE SERVICE STICKER IN A LESS VISIBLE PLACE). I didn’t need to contact the seller for anything because this PC booted up easily. If everyone had my experience I’d say buy without hesitation; I wonder how many of the bad experiences could have been avoided by better packaging? In any event, so far my experience is FANTASTIC FOR THE PRICE :)

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I ordered up 14 of these units (a couple different orders) and started installing them in client locations. Within a week, we started getting calls about the units trying to boot from PXE or saying "Operating System not found." Thought it was a fluke at first but eventually determined that this company has their own white-labeled M.2/PCIe SSDs and this series of Optiplex 7010s do NOT like them. In the end, we ended up having to replace the half dozen or so units we couldn't really swap out with new, brand-name SSDs to resolve the problem.

We did manage to return 7 of them, but I had to go buy big boxes as we'd already tossed the ones they were delivered in. Then we had to hound Amazon for several days to get the seller to actually refund the money (several days in, two of them had been refunded, but Amazon's site just kept saying "Refund in process" and they'd refund the money once they all were received). After a few pokes at Amazon, we did get our money back, but man did this cost me a lot of man hours having to rebuild failed/incompatible SSDs on the fly.

I don't know what's wrong with their white-labeled SSDs, but they must be incredibly cheap (and modern Optiplex units only really like NVMe models that can run in native RAID mode).

For the record, I did go to their web site and it looks like it was done in Microsoft Word. I managed to get a request out explaining my situation but only got a "please create a ticket" response.

I'd used OEMGENUINE in the past with good results, but wow was this a disaster. Do NOT buy these units unless you intend to put a quality SSD in it!!

text:
Purchasing a new computer should be a straightforward and satisfying experience, especially when buying a pre-configured system from a well-known brand like Dell. Unfortunately, my recent purchase of the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF from Green Tech Computers via Amazon has been anything but. What was supposed to be a reliable mini-server for my home office turned into a costly and frustrating ordeal filled with endless troubleshooting, unhelpful customer service, and a product that remains completely unusable.

Below, I’ve outlined my entire experience in detail to ensure others are aware of the challenges I faced and can make an informed decision before purchasing from this seller.

Initial Impressions and Setup
When I first received the Dell OptiPlex 5050 SFF, I was optimistic. The compact design and reputation of the OptiPlex series made it a great fit for my intended use as a mini-server for home projects. However, my optimism quickly faded once I powered on the machine.

From the start, I encountered a critical issue: the system was completely non-functional for basic tasks. I was unable to open browsers, download files, or install any updates. This wasn’t a minor glitch or software hiccup—these are basic functions that any modern computer, let alone a Dell-branded device, should be able to perform right out of the box.

Troubleshooting and Escalation
Recognizing that this wasn’t a typical setup issue, I began an extensive troubleshooting process to identify and resolve the problem. Below is a detailed timeline of my efforts:

1. Initial Troubleshooting Steps
I started by testing the system with standard diagnostics:

Ran Dell Diagnostics: The diagnostics tool reported no hardware issues, which suggested that all components were functioning as intended. However, this was contradicted by the ongoing problems.
Reinstalled Windows: Thinking the issue might be related to the pre-installed OS, I performed a clean installation of Windows 10. Unfortunately, the problems persisted. I couldn’t open browsers, download files, or install updates even after a fresh OS install.
Tested with Linux: I attempted to install Linux as an alternative operating system to bypass potential Windows-related issues. To my shock, the system wouldn’t even proceed to the installation stage, halting abruptly without any clear explanation. The live environment also failed to load. Ubuntu versions16.04, 22.04, 24 and PopOS were used.
2. Communication with Green Tech Computers
Frustrated, I reached out to the seller, Green Tech Computers, for assistance. This began a long and fruitless exchange, documented as follows:

Initial Contact (Dec 21, 2024): I informed them of the 0x80010105 error I was encountering and detailed the issues I was facing. Their response was to apologize and suggest replacing the hard drive, implying that the device had shipped with defective hardware. This was alarming—why would a new product require immediate hardware replacement?

Follow-Up Responses: Over the next several days, I provided them with screenshots of error messages and explained my troubleshooting efforts, including reinstalling Windows and attempting to update drivers. Their replies were repetitive and unhelpful. They insisted that the issue was a missing driver and suggested steps like installing updates via the store or resetting Windows Update components. None of these worked, as the system wouldn’t allow driver installations or updates to proceed.

Contradictory Advice: After reporting the continued failure of their suggestions, they shifted their diagnosis to a "defective system file" or a "Windows activation error." They advised me to download and reinstall Windows from Microsoft’s website—a step I had already performed multiple times without success.

3. Hardware Replacement Attempts
At their suggestion, I replaced the hard drive and memory with new components. I then performed another clean installation of Windows using verified installation media. Despite this, the exact same issues persisted, proving that the problem was not related to the hard drive, memory, or installation media. This confirmed that the root cause was likely a fundamental flaw in the system’s hardware or firmware.

Escalating Frustration
Poor Customer Service from Green Tech Computers
One of the most frustrating aspects of this experience was the lack of accountability or meaningful support from Green Tech Computers. Their responses were generic, dismissive, and showed little regard for the time and effort I invested in troubleshooting their faulty product. Even after replacing hardware and documenting every step of my process, their only advice was to repeat steps I had already tried or refer me back to Amazon.

Warranty Denial
To make matters worse, they refused to honor the warranty, claiming that the system was outside the 90-day warranty period. This was particularly upsetting as the delay in addressing the issue was due to customs clearance, which was beyond my control. I explained this to them and requested some leniency given the circumstances, but they flatly refused to provide any assistance, leaving me with an unusable system and no recourse.

Key Issues with the Product and Seller
1. Defective Hardware
The core problem with this system appears to be a defect in the hardware or firmware. Despite extensive troubleshooting, including replacing components and reinstalling operating systems, the system remains non-functional. This raises serious concerns about the quality control standards at Green Tech Computers.

2. Misleading Support
Throughout my correspondence with Green Tech Computers, their advice was inconsistent and unhelpful. They repeatedly blamed the issue on missing drivers or corrupted files without offering a concrete resolution. Their unwillingness to escalate the issue or take responsibility was unacceptable.

3. Warranty Limitations
Refusing to honor the warranty due to a minor delay caused by customs is an example of poor customer care. Given that the system was clearly defective from the start, Green Tech Computers should have taken ownership of the issue and offered a replacement or refund.

4. Financial Loss
In addition to the cost of the system itself, I incurred additional expenses for replacement hardware (hard drive and memory) and hours of lost time trying to resolve the issue. The total financial and emotional toll of this experience far exceeds the value of the product.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Two things to note, I don't often review products, and I specifically selected STG as the reseller given their positive reviews over the last 12 months, even though I paid $2.00 more and also had to wait an extra day or two for their shipping, it was well worth it.

Not to sound harsh but we as consumers should take some responsibility of what we are purchasing are also specifically who is the reseller, especially when you are buying a refurbished item. You are generally always presented with the cheapest purchase option, that doesn’t mean it is your best option, especially when it comes to refurbished items like PC’s. Keep in mind, this is not a brand-new sparkly PC with a $2K price tag, in the best-case scenario, you are buying a 5-year-old PC, that hopefully was sitting on some drones desk in nice clean office environment, which has now depreciated and is being re-sold back into the mainstream consumer market. The most important part of this process is the cleaning up, reconfiguring and packaging of the PC from its previous life to now being in your most likely, home environment.

STG did a great job of this, the PC was dust free inside, was in pristine condition and from what I can tell, they even put in a new battery on the motherboard (this is to keep the bios going when unplugged, it’s a small battery most people don’t even know exist). It was well packaged, included a very easy to follow single page guide to get Windows activated with Microsoft and they even included a keyboard and mouse for folks who might need it to get started. I will note that the PC itself only has 3 - Display Ports, I missed that in the description but that is on me, not an issue for most people so I just added an HDMI dongle. On a side note, yes, it does have plenty of USB ports, on the front and back, but also has the old school PS/2 style ports available for a mouse and keyboard for nostalgia's sake...ironically, I still have an old trackball mouse that would work on this thing lol.

After getting Windows activated, I immediately added a 2TB NVME drive for the boot drive and cloned the original 1TB SSD through Acronis, which is free to use if you use a Western Digital drive. I then added a dual port 10GB SFP+ network card, an additional 3.5” SATA drive for more storage which I had sitting around, and then added two 16GB DDR4 RAM sticks to get it up to a total of 64GB of RAM. I could not find the exact ADATA ones that came with it, but I did match up the RAM’s speed, voltage and timings to make sure it would work, and it did. Also, I did update the BIOS and some other items from Dell’s website but most people will never need to do this, and in all honesty shouldn’t. I would recommend the RAM I bought but I honestly don't know if it is the same as what came in yours and it may do more harm than good.

This is the first PC I have purchased in about 30 years, I have been building my own since I was a kid in the 90’s but I really just needed a decent PC I could RDP into, use as a management device for my network rack, and also serve as a VM host device using VirtualBox with an Ubuntu and Linux Mint VM. I know Dell is pretty solid when it comes to desktops like these, which are usually targeted at businesses, so my hope is that it just sits in my basement next to the network rack for another 5 years, if it is still running after that, it will just become a full blown linux box.

This is a great little PC as is, but with a few upgrades can be a utility device like what I did, or a light little gaming rig assuming you upgrade the PSU or get a GPU that doesn't need a lot of space or power. Just understand, this is never going to be something you overclock or turn into a 4K 120fps gaming rig, it just doesn't have the space or backbone for it, nor was it ever intended to. It draws very little power, has a nice quiet case and does have WiFi and BT built in if you need it.

Once again, I cannot say enough good things about STG, they did a great job and I would have no problems buying from them again. It was nice to see a seller actually take pride in what they sent, as always, it was the little things that made a big difference for the user/consumer experience!

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Stay away from Tek Refurbs. Full stop.
I ordered 10 refurbished Dell systems for the church where I work, expecting uniform, business-class machines suitable for deployment. What I received was a bait-and-switch disaster.
Every single unit had a replacement motherboard that did not match the model sold. These were not minor revisions — they were entirely different platforms stuffed into the wrong chassis. As a result:
BIOS updates for the advertised model cannot be applied
Chipset and firmware updates must be guessed and manually matched to the actual motherboard
Dell will not provide correct drivers because the service tag no longer matches the hardware
Systems appear functional at first glance but break in subtle, time-consuming ways (USB devices, cameras, firmware management, etc.)
Out of the box, these machines were not fit for business use. They were either unusable or required hours upon hours of deep technical troubleshooting per machine just to reach basic stability. This is completely unacceptable for equipment marketed as refurbished business desktops.
This isn’t normal refurbishment. This is Frankenstein hardware — mismatched boards, wrong firmware paths, and no supportability. If you’re not an experienced systems engineer with time to burn, these machines will waste your time, your money, and your sanity.
Tek Refurbs refused to take responsibility once outside their short return window, despite the issue being hardware misrepresentation, not wear and tear. They are great with copy/pasting the notice that I was outside the return window. No integrity whatsoever though.
If you value:
your time
consistent hardware
the ability to update BIOS and drivers
or any form of vendor accountability
Do not buy from Tek Refurbs.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'd had a Lenovo AIO since early 2016 that was suffering under the twin strains of old age and constant Zoom meetings. There's a huge range of prices and features among available AIOs and much better screen/hard drive options than there was in '16. I wound up paying less than I had then while picking up the three things most important to me: a solid-state drive (to increase retrieval speed and eliminate machine noise during video conferences), the AMD Ryzen 5 processor, and lots of RAM. Another plus is the built-in DVD drive.

The new Lenovo is terrific: fast, quiet, and up to all of the general productivity, light graphics and data processing tasks I require. The touch screen is crisp and clear. The camera, located at the top center of the bezel, is not the best, but it's fine for 1080p and lower levels of resolution. Low-light photography is acceptable (in addition to video calls, I use this camera to record television press interviews; commercial stations have been satisfied with the quality). I also appreciate the physical lens blocker built into the housing of the computer.

I swapped the corded keyboard and mouse for cordless models -- a big reason to have an AIO is to reduce cable clutter -- but noted during setup that both were precise and the keyboard is clicky, a pleasure to type on. Packaging is minimal and operation couldn't be easier; I was up and running within minutes of taking the machine out of its box. The stand, a curved metal tube, it elegant and minimal. I've seen some users complain that the stand doesn't keep the screen straight: I've had no such problems.

All-in-all, I'm very satisfied with the computer, it's a terrific value.

I purchased a Dell 5060 mini computer, and my experience has been deeply frustrating due to several critical issues with the device and the seller's practices:

Incorrect and Underpowered Power Supply: The device was shipped with an aftermarket 45-watt power supply, far below the manufacturer-recommended 90 watts. This causes a BIOS warning at startup, indicating insufficient power, which negatively impacts the device's performance.

Poorly Fitting Barrel Connector: The power supply's barrel connector is a poor fit, leading to frequent disconnections if the device is moved even slightly. This resulted in an unexpected power loss during a reboot, which could have caused data loss or hardware damage.

Deceptive Practices by the Seller: The seller had hidden the BIOS power supply warning by configuring it to be suppressed (accessible by pressing F1), masking the issue at the time of purchase. This prevented me from identifying the problem immediately.

Unresponsive Customer Support: When I contacted the seller about the incorrect power supply, they dismissed my concerns, stating the device was 30 days out of warranty. I argued that this was not a warranty issue but a case of shipping the wrong part, yet they refused to provide any support or resolution.

Unethical Business Practices: I believe the seller knowingly shipped the Dell 5060 with an inadequate power supply, engaging in deceptive practices to hide the issue. This reflects extremely poor business ethics.

Overall, the Dell 5060 I received was compromised by a substandard power supply, leading to unreliable performance and potential risks to the device. And this unit is fast! Everything starts and loads seemingly instantly. Love, love, love that!

So, as should be obvious, we are very, very happy with this unit and would certainly recommend it to others. And, yes, our computer guy is looking at buying several to upgrade his workspace. That tells me a lot.

text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
I got the Dell Inspiron 5645 for Amazon Prime Day in July 2024. Since then this has been a good computer. The price was around $815, which included a protection plan, and I'd say it was worth the price. Most notably, it's more than 5 times faster than my previous fastest computer, which is really great. I put Linux on it and it has run well, though in the last month or two it's been a little glitchy. As of today it's been able to run all my Steam games, as well as a virtual machine for Windows 10.

 I have only two real complaints about it: the computer has only 2 USB A ports and only one slot for a disk drive.

 My previous computer was a Dell Inspiron 3505 I got in 2021. It had 3 USB A ports and two slots for disk drives, and only cost about $300.

 I got the 5645 on Prime Day, but I had found out it was Prime Day only about 4 or 5 hours before it ended. I had a number of things to research in that time, so I didn't really look into the 5645 as thoroughly as I'd have liked. But once I got it and discovered it only had the 2 USB's and 1 storage slot I decided I should probably send it back and get a better machine. But after a week or two of researching it didn't really seem like there was a better laptop available around that price. Apparently the laptop industry has largely decided to only put 1 storage slot and 2 USB A's in their laptops, which I consider very awful.

So I ended up keeping it.

 The lack of a second storage slot and 3rd USB A made it extremely difficult for me to install Linux (which I did largely to avoid Windows Recall). It was the first time I'd installed Linux, but these hardware limitations made it far more difficult than it should have been.

 Overall I do recommend this machine. Just know that in some regards laptop hardware quality seems lesser than it used to be.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'm a fan of the WD 19 family of Dell Docking Stations. I use the WD19DCS in my office set-up which is a more powerful version of the same docking station so I am quite familiar with their capabilities.

I ordered this for use in my home office and was anxious to get it setup. So I unboxed it immediately upon receiving and noticed 2 additional ports which the DCS doesn't have. I didn't recall seeing them in the photos of the WD 19S on Amazon so I checked. Indeed they are not there. Assuming that the pictures were incorrect in the product description on Amazon I looked it up on Dell's website. The listing on Amazon was not wrong the WD 19S does not have the additional 2 ports that the 1 I received has. How could that be? Looking up the service tag on the part I received gave me the answer. I had been sent by the vendor the older original WD 19 model. I then started to wonder what other differences may exist. None. Everything else is the same. Seems during the pandemic Dell was having trouble getting the audio out components for the dock (To be precise one is an audio out jack. the other a headphone jack). Since everything else is the same, I decided not to bring it to anyone's attention.

This dock works perfectly. Since I'm using it most of the time at home with a Lenovo laptop (with 2 monitors) the power button on the top of the dock doesn't work (to be expected) and the dock can only deliver 90W to the laptop (also expected). However, if I plug my phone into the USB-C Gen 2 port it'll super fast charge (requiring 45W) at the same time my Lenovo Yoga also fast charges. That's a bonus. My one regret is that while my WD 19DCS' USB-A ports are Gen 2 (10Gbps transfer rate) this model has only USB-A Gen 1 ports (5Gbps) so data transfers are slower at home than in the office.

I still feel this dock is rock solid and if you don't have need for the faster ports this deck is worth its price.

text: I wanted an improvement over my ten year old 17" monitor and this appears to be the only bargain monitor in the so-called 'square' format, which I prefer as I never play games or watch tv on it. To correct a couple of items - the width is 410 mm, not 457; the height is 412. The base clips together simply and the flat base is useful for putting things on, so little desk space is lost. It plugged and played but only has VGA, there is no DVi socket or lead as stated. I found the increased picture size an advantage for desk top publishing or handling photos and although I was alarmed by the brightness at first (initially reducing it to nearly 0) I found I had made a mistake in increasing the contrast. Lowering the contrast to 65 and setting the brightness to 45 suited both text and photos for me and details emerged I hadn't seen on my previous monitor, which I had probably also set with too much contrast. I am hoping my eyes will suffer less tiredness now. The quality seems excellent and I am still exploring the other settings. text: If you search online for Dell XPS 8940 (mine is the i7 11th generation), you will find loads of links complaining about overheating. Basically the i9 is ok (because it has this actual cooler tower fitted as standard) but the i7 has the same basic pancake cooler as i3 or i5, which is woeful. After doing my homework first, watching some great YouTube videos I was feeling comfortable that this upgrade would work (and for <£40 it was a no-brainer). I believe that this is the exact OEM supplier for Dell and it arrived 4 days early so I was very pleased. Boxed well with polystyrene squares keeping it well protected. The great thing about this cooler is that it is made to fit the Dell proprietary holes (fits perfectly straight out of the box), it comes already with a rectangular even layer of thermal paste covered by a green plastic shield. Note: I also bought a bottle 99.9% alcohol and special cloths to clean off the old thermal paste. Watch the YouTube videos and you cannot go wrong even for a novice. CPU temps were 70-90c and now down to 40-60c, so pleased. I did not even need to change the stock rear case fan. Note: Good idea to also get a VRM Heat sink also from Amazon. A great project and so worth doing. The pc is now faster as well because the CPU is not throttling down.

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Several issues with this CPU fan/heatsink for my Dell 7040, although I was able to hack together a workable solution, so I’m giving it two stars.

The heatsink is smaller than the original, with less surface area for heat dissipation, although the screw positions are compatible. More importantly, the fan screw holes are on the opposite side of the board screws, which means the plastic airflow shroud cannot be used. See the attached pictures showing both issues.

Since I needed a quick fix and did not want to wait for a replacement, I removed the new fan from its heatsink and mounted it onto the original heatsink instead. During that process, it was obvious that the plastic on the replacement fan was lower quality than the original (thinner and feels brittle). The fan mounting hole spacing was also slightly different, but close enough that I was able to install it.

Fortunately, I had good-quality thermal paste on hand, since reinstalling the original heatsink required fresh paste for proper heat transfer.

After this modification, the fan powered up and worked properly. It is somewhat louder than the original fan, but not by much.

The Dell 7040 is an older computer, so I do appreciate that this replacement part is available (and it may fit other Dell models). However, for my 7040, if I need to repair it again, I would source only the fan rather than this fan/heatsink assembly.

If you're not sure what drill bit to use, I'll share the tip I looked up. It's a bit of guessing. Take whatever drill bit you think you'll need and hold it flat in front of the screw you have. The ONLY thing you should see of the screw behind the bit is the threads. So if your bit is to big or too small, keep picking bits in the right direction until all you can see are the threads of the screw and the bit seems to match the center of the screw.

I have attached my UPS to the back underside of my standing desk. This mount worked very well. I purposely left a gap at the top because my UPS has vents on the top. Most computers don't, so you can secure them tightly to the top which will keep them from moving.

I'm a little concerned about the plastic buckles through which the straps are passed to reverse them and allow the velcro (hook and loop) closure to hold the desired length. This mount apparently is rated for up to 100 lbs, so my 25 lb UPS should be no problem. Still, I would have preferred to see them use metal.

The instructions are not helpful in choosing which set of straps to use (there's a set for larger and a set for smaller devices), so I selected the right ones by trial and error. The instructions also don't indicate which way the straps should face when lacing them through the slots (the velcro loop side should be facing away from the device you're hanging). Again, trial and error reveals the right thing to do, but that's what instructions are supposed to do for us.

This is an inexpensive mount that does just what you want. It can hold things vertically or horizontally. It doesn't rotate or slide. It just holds things in a fixed position well. If the straps hold like they are supposed to, and the instructions improve, this is worth five stars.

(BTW, I mounted my UPS at the same end of my standing desk as my computer. The extra weight at the one end was, in retrospect, unwise. The desk wobbles a little now when it moves. One of these days, I'm going to swap it to the other end. Keep that in mind if you decide to do what I've done.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I needed:
I needed a computer for my electronics lab. It didn't need to be immensely powerful, but I wanted something that would be easy to expand as needed. This PC met my needs almost perfectly, and at a very economical price. I purchased this 6 months ago (almost to the day), so this is not an "out of the box" impression, but one based on months of experience. It has been powered on (or sleeping) continuously, so I can remote access it when needed.

My uses are primarily centered around my lab work: Electronic Design, PCB Layout, and 3D Rendering of PCBs, along with Design of small enclosures and modest software development. I also have several PC connected pieces of bench equipment: Digital Scope, Power Supplies, Function Generator, and whatever thing I'm creating. Most of these connect via USB, and one via RS-232.

This PC:
You can see in the pictures that the front panel has 4 USB ports - 2 are SuperSpeed. These have already proven valuable for quick attachments.

The rear panel is loaded up with 6 more USB ports (2 of which are SuperSpeed), and I've used most of them. If I had to, I could easily dig out an old PS2 Keyboard to free up another USB port - but with 4 empty ports on the front I'm ok for now.

As noted above, I needed RS-232, and this PC had one - which is a bonus. Of course, I could have plugged in a USB to RS-232 adapter. Beneath the back-panel RS-232 port (the gray plug in the picture) is a VGA connector, which I don't expect to use. To the left of those are a couple of Display Ports - one connected to my big screen (3440 x 1440). The specs say that each can support a 4K monitor, but my bench doesn't have space (and the screen resolution works for my eyeballs and needs).

The host processor in the unit I purchased is an i5-4590 quad core running at 3.3 GHz. The motherboard memory slots are full, loaded with 16 GB of RAM. The motherboard has 3 SATA ports, but they are fully occupied, connected to a 240 GB SSD hosting Win10 Pro, a 1GB spinning HDD, and a DVD drive. The graphics is served with an integrated Intel HD 4600. For further expansion, there are 4 PCIe slots: 2 x X1, 1 x X4 and 1 x X16.

Other Discoveries:
* The BIOS still had the name of the prior "owner" (a company), which is probably where many of these came from. It was simple to change, so now is hosts a name appropriate for my lab.
* This PC is not for gaming, so I didn't rate that since I've never run a game on it. With my single high-resolution monitor connected, spinning a 3D model of a modestly complex circuit board is fast - it more than meets my needs.
* And I had no need for Tech Support, so I didn't rate that either.

My Expansion:
* In the pictures you'll see one of the PCI slots is occupied - with the 4-channel SATA adapter that I added. The 3 on the motherboard were occupied but I needed one more for an external HD dock.
* I expect to add a Webcam soon.
* I also expect to add one more PCI card to it, to add USB-C connectors. My newest gear (Laptop, Phone, etc.) all have USB-C, so this will be necessary.

My Summary:
This was the right PC for my needs. It was also relatively inexpensive. It has been running close to non-stop since my unboxing. It "seems" quiet enough for most any location, but my lab isn't the best place to judge that.

It didn't have support for every interface I needed but was more than expandable enough to add to it. I do wish the overall unit was a bit smaller (for my lab space), and in years prior I had a large tower PC, but tired of crawling under the desk to swap cables around.

text:
It was delivered on time and was in like-new condition as advertised. It has a smaller footprint than a full-size desktop which I had concerns about before I got it. However, once I opened the access panel, I was impressed. It has a recessed latched pull handle that removes the whole access panel exposing everything and no screws to unscrew or lose. Inside, not a speck of dust, literally, like a new computer, you can't tell that it's renewed/upgraded.

Even though it's smaller everything is easy to see and get to so if you need or want to do anything inside it's awesome. You can see everything and get to it with ease. You don't have to be a contortionist or have tiny hands and fingers. The drives and optical reader (DVD) are contained within a rack that you just pivot upward to release and you have full easy access to them. Additional expansion slots to add what you like. If you should want to increase RAM from 16 to 32 GB there is nothing around them so removing and replacing them in the slots would be effortless. I was surprised how cool this computer runs even when using multiple high resource software at the same time with no lag.

As for the USB Keyboard and Mouse, USB WiFi Adapter. These are low cost and just so you have something. As low cost as keyboard and mouse are I really like them. If you use something else don't throw them out as others have said. Save them as an emergency back up or give them to someone. I have a Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse but still using the ones that came with this computer. USB WiFi Adapter isn't the best it's not real fast and not great for long-distance so I did buy a better one at the same time. There are a lot of cheap USB WiFi Adapters that stop working after 2-3 months but here is a low-cost $17 good one I use so can avoid the hassle.
Just search amazon for -
TP-Link AC600 USB WiFi Adapter for PC (Archer T2U Plus)- Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop with 2.4GHz, 5GHz High Gain Dual Band 5dBi Antenna, Supports Windows 10/8.1/8/7/XP, Mac OS 10.9-10.14
It increased my transfer speed from 300 Mbps or less and 3 bars signal strength to a transfer speed of 433 to 490 Mbps and 5 bars signal strength.

All you have to do is connect a monitor, the keyboard, mouse, and USB wifi adapter and power up. You do need to set up you user account like any new computer. This is Microsoft so it wants you to use a Microsoft account to have a better "online experience". But all you need to do is enter your login for a Microsoft email account or create one during set up. That step requires connecting to the internet and entering the password. Or you can create an offline user account like the old days. The rest of the setup questions are about your preferences and you're ready to go.

Windows 10 Pro works perfectly. My daughter got one of these a while ago and wouldn't stop praising it so I got one. She gave me a heads up about the USB WiFi Adapter solution too. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.
