title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It's not a huge savings to get this motherboard with Amazon renewed. So I'm not sure it is worth the gamble even though you can return it if broken I'm sure.

First off, I'm very comfortable putting computers and servers together. I often buy used server hardware and it has all sorts of missing parts, dirt, dust, etc.

I picked up this MSI motherboard renewed and it had some thermal paste on the socket. I don't think it was enough to be a problem, but I cleaned it out carefully with a toothpick and some rubbing alcohol on a cloth wiping the surface. Then the back of the board also had thermal paste on it even more so. Someone must have had it all over their hands when handling the board is my only thought. Again, easy to clean up, but why wasn't it cleaned in the first place?

So I wish it would have been better cleaned. Also there was a scratch on the io armor, the aluminum which is painted black was showing the metal. I took a sharpie and made it blend in. Not a huge deal, but just the look of the board...it was more used than refurbished.

Typically with a refurb or anything off Amazon renewed I'd expect things to look as new. That's always been my experience. Now the screws and cables were all bagged. So everything else was new and all there (unless a manual was supposed to come with it, but I downloaded the PDF, again no biggie).

...but you kinda look at it and realize for $20 savings, it's a bit of a gamble. The product probably should have been sold as used on eBay for a bigger discount to be frank.

I'm a huge fan of reusing computer parts. Far too much in landfills. However, you are taking a bit of a gamble when doing so. You don't know how something has been handled before.

All that said, so far the motherboard seems fine. It's only been a day, but I expect it to be working just fine.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
First off I have been building my own personal computers since 1983 or so. By far this motherboard tops them all and not just because it has the latest and greatest features, but the fact that the quality and supplied software is very good. I read and read motherboard reviews before settling in buying the MSI Ace. I am sure you are also reading reviews. One major differentiation between MSI and competing motherboard suppliers is their BIOS software. It is frustrating having terrible BIOS software that is either not intuitive or is 'buggy'. I have had 10's of motherboards from other major manufacturers and was never satisfied with their BIOS software. Even if you can find a competing motherboard that may eke out one percentage faster OC capability but has sub par BIOS software, it just is not worth the purchase in my opinion. It seems like I read millions of motherboard reviews and the vast majority of them overlook the software aspect. I did find one review where the guy said he thought the MSI software was 'OK', but I have been using it for the past week, and I love it. From what I have read MSI has been standardizing on their BIOS software vs developing something brand new every time they come out with a new motherboard which to me means they can spend their time fine tuning their existing software.

My build consisted of a MSI Ace Motherboard, i7-9700K Intel Processor, XFX Over Clocked 580RX Video Card, 32GB Corsair Vengeance 3200MHz DRAM, WD Black 500GB m.2 drive, 4TB WD Hard Drive, 500GB Samsung SSD from my prior build, Corsair 570X Crystal Series Glass Mid Tower Case (which is also awesome), a Corsair H115i liquid cooler, Corsiar LL series RGB fans and RGB Light Strips. I absolutely love my system. I was able to easily overclock the processor to 5.2GHz, but settled at 5.1GHz to allow a little headroom. BTW, MSI has an excellent Overclocking guide for the I9 and I7-9700K processor installed on a MSI motherboard. A must read if you want to Overclock. I only have my CPU Core voltage at 1.310 at 5.1GHz, so if you start with the guides recommended 1.37V setting and your overclock works then keep backing down the voltage by .100 volt until your system becomes unstable. Then set the Core CPU voltage to .200 or .300 volts higher than the unstable voltage so you aren't running on the ragged edge. This is what I did on my system and I have been doing some heavy gaming, etc. with zero heating or software problems.

Other thoughts: All the MSI Z390 boards (i.e., Ace, Pro Carbon, Gaming Edge, Godlike, etc.) seem to be similar except for variations in power supplies and USB, Wi-Fi, etc. I choose the Ace due to all of the USB connectors and its 13 phase power supply. I don't think you could go wrong with any of the other MSI motherboards. The i7-9700K processor is great with zero complaints. All of the Corsair products work great. My only partial regret is not going to at least a 2070 or higher series graphic card. No complaints on the 580X with an AMD processor, but just not fast enough for me. My reasoning for not biting the bullet on a +$600 Graphics Card is this: I am attending the 2019 CES show in a couple of weeks and I want to see what's up with AMD's upcoming offering to compete with NVIDIA. Rumors are AMD's new GUI's are going to kick butt, and be less expensive. I know you can spend the rest of your life waiting to pull the trigger on buying a cutting edge Graphics Card, but this time I decided to wait, right or wrong. Since I like my MSI motherboard so much, I will probably end up replacing with a MSI Graphics card. Presetly my system can play most games on Medium or High Setting with FPS varying from 30 to 80 at a 1920 x 1080 resolution. I use a 34" wide Dell 3415W monitor that supports up to 3440 x 1440 resolution, and not being able to take advantage of the monitors full resolution keeps me up at night. LOL So, I am hoping in the next few months their will be a sub $500 MSI graphics card that will allow me to play almost all my games at High or Ultra High settings on my monitors max 3440 x 1440 resolution setting at 50FPS or better. I want to be able to go full throttle for a few years without having to upgrade again.

Tips: If you can't get your wireless mouse to work with the MSI BIOS then plug in a corded USB mouse. I had to do this, though you can use the keyboard to navigate the BIOS without a mouse, just slower for me. Also, you can like or dislike Corsair, but I like their products. Their documentation is sometimes lacking and their pricing a little high, but their quality and breadth of computer kit building hardware is excellent. It's nice to have a company who still sells products for the home PC builder! I built this computer on my kitchen counter height island which is much easier than building on the floor like I have previously done with other computer builds. Just clear off the counter, it is worth it.

Big Tip: If you use the Corsair H115i cooler, the MSI Ace Motherboard, and the Corsair 570X case the cooling radiator will NOT fit on the inside TOP of the case. And, since the radiator is supplied with (2) 140mm LL Series fans, and the top of the Corsair case is the only spot for (2) 140mm fans this creates a big problem, or so I thought. There is not enough room due to the radiator and fan combination interfering with the Motherboard. Needless to say when I discovered this I was in disbelief especially after planning every last detail of my build, plus I already had the Motherboard installed in the case and wired up. I searched the internet for a couple of hours and could not find an easy solution. Some people went to extreme measures to make this combination work, but I didn't want to do any drilling on my brand new case! But, after a couple of beers and staring at my case for a few minutes I found my answer: Mount the radiator on the front of the case. This was fairly simple,; however, you will need to swap the flat metal plate that holds the (3) fans on the front of the case with the plate on top of the case that is made to hold (2) fans. I am not sure if Corsair made the case to be able to do this, but nonetheless it works. Because I wanted to see my funky RGB fans when viewing the front of the case I attached the (2) LL Series Corsair fans that came with the H115i cooler to the front of the case, THEN I mounted the radiator on top of the fans with the supplied longer Corsair screws. As far as the airflow, there should be very little difference. Just make sure the (2) Radiator fans and the Top (3) Case fans are blowing air out of the case. I ended up putting a single LL series RGB 120mm fan on the rear of the case with the air blowing into the case. This is probably not needed, but it looks pretty darn cool.

Last tip: Go for it. When it comes to finally pulling the trigger on all the components for your new computer build don't let a few hundred bucks get in your way. Look at it this way, just cut out a few nights out on the town and use the savings to stay home and admire your PC. Yes, you qualify as being a little nerdy, but no one will know. LOL

Update 9/8/2019: I am still loving this motherboard and have had Zero problems. One tip I can pass along is to make sure you keep the Killer Network software up-to-date. I still haven’t purchased a 2080 video card, but one is still on my list if the prices ever drop! As far as gaming I have been using my Xbox on a 75” UHD TV with a 5.1.4 Atmos sound system. I like this gaming setup better so really no need for super fast graphics on PC, at least for me.

text:
The MSI MAG X670E Tomahawk WiFi Gaming Motherboard is an excellent choice for gamers and PC builders looking for top-tier performance at a reasonable price. It combines powerful features, great build quality, and reliable performance, making it perfect for high-end gaming and content creation.

Build and Design
This motherboard has a sleek, matte black design with durable components. It handles heat extremely well, with solid cooling around the VRM and reinforced PCIe slots to keep the GPU secure.

Performance
The X670E chipset supports the latest AMD Ryzen series CPUs, offering fast speeds and smooth performance (I am using it with a Ryzen 9 7900X). It supports PCIe 5.0, ensuring quick data transfer for your GPU and storage, and it can handle DDR5 RAM up to 6400 MHz (with potential for even higher speeds). The VRM design ensures stable power, even during heavy gaming or overclocking.

Connectivity
The board has Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 for fast and stable wireless connections. For wired setups, it includes 10Gb Ethernet, ideal for online gaming or fast file transfers. It also has four M.2 slots and six SATA ports, so you can easily add storage or expand your build.

Easy Setup and User-Friendly
MSI's BIOS is simple to use, even for beginners, with options for both automatic and manual overclocking. The MSI Dragon Center software allows easy performance monitoring and customization, including RGB lighting.

Durability
Built with military-grade components, the Tomahawk motherboard is designed to last. It also has protection features to keep your system safe from power surges and static damage.

Conclusion
The MSI MAG X670E Tomahawk WiFi offers great value with top performance, a sleek design, and plenty of connectivity options. It’s perfect for anyone building a high-performance gaming PC or workstation and provides everything you need for smooth, reliable performance. If you're looking for a motherboard that can handle the latest AMD processors and demanding tasks, this is an excellent choice.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I built my first PC in early October with the MSI MAG X670E Tomahawk WiFi Gaming Motherboard, pairing it with an AMD 7800X3D CPU, and it’s been fantastic for gaming. This motherboard offers all the features you need for a smooth, high-performance experience. After a month of gaming with it I can comfortably say it works fine, had a few hiccups like issues with the ram speed but I fixed it.

Pros:

Solid Build Quality: The board feels sturdy, with high-quality components that give me confidence in its longevity.
Plenty of SSD Slots: With multiple SSD slots, it’s perfect for anyone needing lots of fast storage options. Especially the PCIe 5.0 slot.
Strong Connectivity & Efficient Cooling: The WiFi 6E connection is stable and fast, and the cooling design keeps everything running cool, even during long gaming sessions. It comes with ssd heat-sinks for the PCIe 5.0 slot and two PCIe 4.0 slots, which is cool if your ssd doesnt have a manufacturer heat-sink. I will also mention you should always try to use an Ethernet cable before WiFi, but if you cant this motherboard doesn't disappoint.

Slight Pro:

Convenient BIOS Reset: The easy BIOS reset pin is incredibly handy for beginners, it can be a little intimidating, but I appreciate the quick access of its location. If anything happens, all it takes is a screwdriver to short-circuit the pins to reset.

Minor Con: One of the SSD slots is located behind the GPU area, which isn’t the most accessible, especially if you have a beefy GPU like the 7900 XTX. However, with the extra slots available, this isn’t hardly a big issue. There is also no paper manual included, its a little fustraiting when building for the first time and all your other parts do the same thing and give you a QR code to scan and you have swap browsers and such when you all you could do is just grab the paper.

Overall, the MSI MAG X670E Tomahawk WiFi is an excellent choice for first-time builders like myself and/or seasoned gamers. It combines ease of setup, great features, and strong performance. Of course, do your research on compatible components, PC Part picker is a great site to use for looking at things like that. I highly recommend this motherboard!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a solid motherboard that I got refurbished on the cheap. I love refurbished tech as it's always like a brand new item for much less.
This motherboard has BCLK OC, is stable when a 13600kf is OCd but you'll probably want an AIO 360 for temps, handles XMP perfectly and I can't find anything wrong with it. My CPU idle power consumption is much less than a Gigabyte AC DDR5 Z790 motherboard I used prior. The Gigabyte idled at 20w for some reason but the same settings when using the MSI gave me a nice 5-8w idle on average. That's incredible for a fast higher TDP 13600kf CPU, so I'm very satisfied. I would highly recommend this to anybody needing a new motherboard. DDR4 isn't an issue since there's not a huge difference when using P/E CPUs in real world applications. The only real benefit to DDR5 might be the iGPU by a bit or AI apps that are using CPU with memory instead of a dGPU using VRAM, but even with DDR4 the iGPU would work perfect for something like JellyFin or Handbrake and you will only really notice the difference when using synthetic benchmarking software. Plus, gaming isn't ever recommended when using the UHD 770 regardless of memory type. Most users don't need DDR5 with 12th-14th gen CPUs since AI software primarily uses dGPU cores and memory to get the task done. Gaming doesn't yield good improvements when using DDR5 either. Average users of AI probably won't be using CPU based AI since it's much slower even when using DDR5 and requires an expensive amount of memory so it doesn't use the page/swap file/partition. DDR5 is best for the newer Core Ultra CPUs due to better iGPUs and being quite different, so if you want to save some $$$ then this motherboard will definitely help accomplish that while not sacrificing performance. The WiFi module is fast and I can easily use all of my 400mbps internet speed. It can handle over gigabit speeds too and my local transfers are very fast. Even faster than my Ethernet connections.

Also take note, after flashing to a newer BIOS in 2025 the BCLK feature is still there. This is great! Some vendors removed this feature when people updated their BIOS so I'm glad MSI kept it with this board in case I needed it. Many Z790 motherboards don't even have this feature from what I've seen.

Keep it up MSI!!

text:
The board looks nice, has decent features, but be aware of these limitations:
1) If you take advantage of the WiFi feature, you will lose the 2nd M2 slot, since the wifi module uses that slot
2) If you use the 2nd M2 slot for a SATA drive rather than an NVME drive, you lose SATA connecter 8 on the mother board
3) There is no video port (typically HDMI) on this board, so it requires a separate video card
4) Amazon's description of maximum memory is incorrect (64GB). It's actually 192GB
5) On all MSI B760 boards, the connectors for HDD LED, Reset, Power, and Power LED are in a tiny corner all together which makes it miserable to get these connectors once it's placed in the case

If you can live with these limitations, it's a fine board, and apparently all MSI boards are on sale now, so it's a great time to buy.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
These are very good boards. I have 2 holding Ryzen 5 3600x and three carrying Ryzen 5 3600. Running 16 gb of 3200 Ghx memory. Adjusted the timings and have them at 3400 now. Have not OC'd the CPUs b/c these are work computers. Installed cheap 2 Gb graphics cards with Evo 970s (@M.2#1)and 10 Gbase-t cards.

Basic Input-Output system is easy to use but you can easily brick the things with bad memory timings. But un-bricking is easy: kill the power, pull the power cable , pop the battery out and and hold the power button down to discharge any capacitors (ten seconds). Put the battery back and start over. Don't be afraid of memory timings. Keep playing with them until everything works well.

Ignore CPU power 2 BTW (not needed).

M.2 was easy but be SURE you are using the supplied standoffs and screws. Then the heat spreader will lay over the whole thing nicely (at 1st M.2 position). M.2#2 has no heat spreader and is unused on my boards.

No surprises with PCIe cards. The 2 Gb hound of a graphics card sits at the first slot and the 10 Gb ethernet at the second PCIe16.

Cpu/fan mounting was trivially simple.

These things can come together in 10 minutes or less.

That's all I have to report.

text:
You honestly can't get anything better than the MSI MPG Z790 Edge Wifi motherboard. As someone invested in MSI products, it's safe to say I'm a little bit biased, but this motherboard has all of the bells and whistles you could possibly need. I bought it due to it supporting 12th and 13th gen intel CPUs as well as DDR5. I intend to keep this PC build, and hence the motherboard for a long time, so I wanted to future proof a bit.

The BIOS was a little lackluster - as I couldn't find a way to manually select booting from my 2TB M.2 SSD, although it was recognized. Unplugging the 2.5" SSD rectified the issue and allowed me to install windows directly to the M.2 (although it still didn't show clearly in the boot order). Other than this the BIOS is intuitive and user-friendly.

The build quality of the board is very nice, overall I have no complaints and it holds up well so far - (I admit to a minor unintentional drop and it sounded rough, but nothing broke and there's no issues.) The labeling is intuitive, and you have many, many plugs and ports. (you'll never realistically be able to use all of the M.2's and SATAs, but you have options for many drives if you have an extensive game library.)

My two chief complaints with this motherboard are the instructions in the box and the price. The instructions are vague, uninformative and have no words - only pictures and QR codes that link you to videos (which are somewhat helpful but just give me a description!). I highly recommend going to MSI's website and downloading the full user manual for your motherboard, as it will answer all your questions. Regarding price: you can buy other, less flashy motherboards for significantly less than I paid. Even more so if you stick to DDR4 motherboards. My desire to future proof and use MSI however, convinced me to pay the price I did.

Overall, great motherboard. It's sleek, has an RGB gaming dragon logo integrated into it, has an ez debugging LED system (very useful), and a pretty easy to use BIOS. I will come back to update this in the future if anything arises.

Edit: I came back just to say I still haven't had any issues with this motherboard. Absolutely solid purchase and I stand by it almost 3 years later.

text:
هذه لوحة Z790 رائعة تتمتع بتصميم ممتاز وأداء قوي، وهي تعد خيارًا ممتازًا للمستخدمين الذين يبحثون عن قيمة جيدة في فئة لوحات Z790. على الرغم من أنها ليست من سلسلة MEG مثل بعض اللوحات الأخرى في السوق، إلا أنها تتميز بمزايا قد تجعلها الأفضل في فئتها. إليكم تفاصيل تجربتي معها:

التصميم والمظهر: اللوحة تأتي بتصميم أنيق بلون فضي يميل إلى البياض، مما يجعلها تناسب معظم صناديق الكمبيوتر، خاصة إذا كانت لديك مكونات بيضاء. عرضتها في صندوق كمبيوتر أبيض مع بطاقة رسومات 4090 FE، وبدت لوحة Z790 تتناغم بشكل جيد مع باقي المكونات.

الإضاءة RGB: اللوحة لا تحتوي على إضاءة RGB مدمجة بشكل كبير، لكنها مزودة برأس RGB بجهد 5 فولت. الإضاءة تقتصر على مؤشرات أخطاء في اللوحة، ما يجعلها خيارًا جيدًا للمستخدمين الذين لا يهتمون بالإضاءة الزائدة أو يفضلون التحكم الكامل في الإضاءة من خلال مكونات أخرى مثل ذاكرة الوصول العشوائي أو المراوح.

التخزين: تقدم اللوحة خيارات تخزين مميزة مع 3 منافذ M.2، اثنان منها يدعمان الجيل الرابع وواحد يدعم الجيل الثالث. هذا التنوع يوفر مرونة كبيرة في تركيب الأقراص الصلبة ذات الأداء العالي. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، يوجد منفذ SATA يمكن استخدامه لإضافة أقراص إضافية، مما يجعلها مثالية للأجهزة الصغيرة مثل ITX.

جودة البناء: تم بناء اللوحة بشكل متين، مع تفاصيل تجعلها تتفوق على بعض لوحات Edge الأخرى. على الرغم من عدم وجود لوحة خلفية كاملة، فإن الهيكل العام يقدم صلابة كبيرة، وهو ما يساعد في استقرار النظام أثناء رفع تردد التشغيل. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، تم تحسين الأداء في رفع تردد التشغيل على الذاكرة، مما يجعلها خيارًا ممتازًا لمحبي رفع الأداء.

الضوضاء: مقارنة ببعض اللوحات الأخرى، قد تجد أن مستوى الضوضاء في اللوحة أعلى قليلاً. ولكن من تجربتي، كان الصوت أكثر وضوحًا في بعض الأحيان، خاصة عند تشغيل التبريد النشط. قد لا يكون هذا مزعجًا في بيئات غير صامتة تمامًا، ولكنه قد يكون ملحوظًا في أماكن هادئة.

رفع تردد التشغيل: أداء اللوحة في رفع تردد التشغيل مميز جدًا. جربت مع ذاكرة Hynix A التي تبلغ سرعتها 7000 CL34 و 7200 CL34، وتمكنت من دفع السرعة إلى 7800 و8000 بسهولة. حتى مع رفع الفولتية إلى 1.5 فولت، تبقى درجات الحرارة تحت السيطرة (أقل من 55 درجة مئوية)، وهو ما يضمن أداء مستقرًا. إضافة إلى ذلك، كان المعالج 13600K قادرًا على الوصول إلى 5.7 جيجاهرتز بسهولة.

الفولتية وتوصيل الطاقة: اللوحة توفر طاقة مستقرة، حيث يعمل المعالج 13600K مع فولتية 1.18 فولت بشكل طبيعي. ويمكن زيادة الجهد حتى 1.4 فولت بشكل افتراضي مما يساعد على استقرار الأداء في حالات الضغط. مع ذلك، ينصح بتعديل الجهد للحصول على أفضل أداء حسب نوع الشريحة التي تستخدمها.

درجات الحرارة: أثناء استخدام اللوحة مع معالجات عالية الأداء مثل 13600K و13900K، قد ترتفع درجات حرارة اللوحة بعض الشيء، خاصة في منطقة PCH. إذا كنت تستخدم تبريد AIO بدون تدفق هواء جيد على اللوحة، فقد تواجه بعض الارتفاعات في درجة الحرارة. ومع ذلك، تظل درجات الحرارة ضمن الحدود المقبولة، ولا تشكل مشكلة كبيرة إذا كان لديك تدفق هواء جيد.

العيوب: النقطة السلبية الوحيدة في هذه اللوحة هي عدم دعمها لتقنية Thunderbolt. إذا كنت بحاجة إلى دعم Thunderbolt، فإن هذه اللوحة لن تكون الخيار المثالي لك.

الخلاصة: بشكل عام، تعتبر هذه اللوحة واحدة من أفضل الخيارات في فئة Z790. تتميز بجودة بناء عالية، وأداء متميز في رفع تردد التشغيل، ومرونة في التخزين. إذا لم تكن بحاجة إلى دعم Thunderbolt، فهي تعد من أفضل الخيارات من حيث القيمة مقابل المال.

هذه اللوحة هو توازنها الرائع بين الأداء والسعر إنها توفر مميزات ممتازة مثل دعم الذاكرة DDR5 بسرعة عالية، مع قدرة كبيرة على رفع تردد التشغيل، مما يتيح للمستخدمين الحصول على أداء متميز في الألعاب والتطبيقات الثقيلة. كما أنها توفر خيارات تخزين ممتازة مع دعم ثلاث منافذ 2.M، اثنان منها يدعمان الجيل الرابع، مما يوفر سرعة نقل بيانات عالية. أيضًا، تصميم اللوحة أنيق، مع تناغم جيد مع الأجزاء الأخرى خاصة إذا كنت تستخدم صندوق كمبيوتر أبيض الإضاءة RGB المحدودة هي ميزة لبعض المستخدمين الذين يفضلون التركيز على الأداء دون التشتت بالأضواء

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I had an issue with install - no display and no posting to bios. After flashing the bios to the latest version, it posted fine with display and stable through stress testing. Steps below.

CPU: Intel Core i5-12600KF LGA1700 600
CPU Cooler: Thermaltake TH240 ARGB All-in-One Liquid Cooling System 240mm CL-W286-PL12SW-C
Motherboard: MSI PRO Z690-A WiFi ProSeries Motherboard
Storage: WD_BLACK 1TB SN850 NVMe WDS100T1X0E
Memory: TEAMGROUP T-Force Vulcan DDR5 Ram 32GB 5200MHz FLBD532G5200HC40CDC01
PSU: Thermaltake Toughpower PF1 850W 80+ Platinum PS-TPD-0850FNFAPU-1
GPU: 1070 - swapping to RX 6700 XT
--------------------------------

This is a great DDR 5 board. Looks good, but, missing a lot of bells and whistles you don't need anyway for gaming. This is the best budget gaming motherboard to pair with DDR5 memory. I paired this with 32gb Vulcan memory for $200 less than the next mb/memory combo.

Getting download speeds of 450+ (max under my service provider) in the room furthest away from my router on a different house level.

When I first installed this board, I was getting no display no posting to the bios. The LED troubleshooting lights were flashing cpu then solid green on boot. I was afraid the board was DOA.I started running through troubleshooting steps. 

I checked the power connections, made sure my CPU was set correctly and went to one stick in dimm A2 (as outlined in manual). The kf chip does not have integrated graphics so swapped to a GPU I knew was working 1070. Still no post.

I opts to flash the bios using the bios flash port. search for "MSI® HOW TO use Flash BIOS Button"
Flash your bios at your own risk, but these steps worked for me.

1. using a different device, I download latest bios to usb drive (8gb+ formatted to fat 32) 
2. renamed bios file to msi.rom.
3. plugged usb drive to flash bios port
4. with power off (psu hooked into CPU_pwr1 and ATX pwr1 and plugged into the outlet)
5. Hit flash bios button
6. usb drive and lights on mb flash/blink during installation (do not mess with board during this). Board will restart a few times when finished and lights will turn off. 
7. Install CPU, GPU, cooling, memory if needed.

Bios posted and I was able to install windows and it has passed every stress test so far. Works great and very stable/fast. If you run into issues don't give up just yet. This is a new board with new architecture. you may need to update the bios if you run into issues. At time of this review, you will not find a cheaper wifi ddr5 board through amazon.

This is an inexpensive Z690 motherboard for those who want some room for mild overclocking. I only planned to use air cooling and only do mild overclocking so all the extra features of the higher-priced boards are unnecessary for my use.

It has PCIe 5.0, but it is likely the next generation of GPUs won't utilize this. However, I do expect this to get utilized before the natural lifespan of this board. Intel has confirmed Gen 13 CPUs will Socket 1700, and it is generally understood that Gen 14 will also (no official statement on Gen 14 CPUs as far as I know).

DDR5 will become the standard and likely be utilized more with Intel Gen 13. PC5600 will be a part of the JEDEC standard for 13th Gen CPUs.

Now for the gripes: Why on earth are motherboard makers sending optical disks with drivers? Absolutely terrible practice. You better have a LAN cable to do a fresh install because you can't use WiFi out of the box even on Windows 11 installers. This doesn't bother me excessively, but I could see this being an issue for many buyers.

The BIOS has been and continues to be MSI's weakest point. I'm used to it, so that doesn't bother me as much but it really could use a revamp.

Overall: Excellent motherboard especially when you consider cost. Handles minor overclocking without issue. I think MSI should charge the extra $5 for USB sticks with drivers on them.

text:
Thought I'd just leave this here for anyone in a similar situation to myself- upgraded from a 10th gen i5 to a 14th gen i7, so was left with the dilemma of the Z690 chipset being too new to support my 10th gen but simultaneously not being new enough to support my 14th gen CPU (without a BIOS update, that is). Had to use the flash BIOS button on the board itself but had never done so before and was terrified of bricking the board or not being able to flash it at all, since there was no way for my system to POST, let alone boot.
1) Ensure that your drive is formatted to FAT32 (most guides will mention this), AND the partition is MBR, NOT GPT. The manual did not mention requiring the partition to be MBR, only that the format had to be FAT32.
2) Ensure that you pick the right driver (don't pick the DDR4 version accidentally or the Z690-P version, for instance), and ensure you rename the file to MSI.ROM with file extensions already visible, so it doesn't end up being MSI.ROM.AG0 or w/e.
3) Every video and guide that I watched/read, all mentioned that the flashing process would take somewhere between 2-8 minutes, with your only indication being a flashing red light that would stop flashing when the process was complete. If the red light flashes about 3 times or so and stops- it didn't work. Something went wrong in step 1 or 2.
That said, my BIOS flashing process only took about 30 seconds, so I panicked and wasn't sure if it had failed or not, but upon assembling my system outside of my case, it managed to POST so it had worked. ONE single thread that I found mentioned that you can be 'one of the lucky ones' whose BIOS would be successfully flashed in ~30 seconds.
4) When my PC DID finally POST & boot, it wouldn't recognise my new gen 4 NVMe M.2 nor my new GPU. I was scratching my head for a good while wondering if something wasn't connected right, if only 4 pins was connected instead of 8... but as it turns out, despite downloading the latest BIOS build (2024-01-24 as of this review), it only updated to the 2023-09-12 build, which was the first build to support 14th Gen Intel CPUs. So all I had to do was flash my BIOS via M-FLASH in the BIOS itself this time, and everything worked just fine. I'm sure there's a reason it's done this way- but I'm writing this here so you, the person reading this, doesn't end up panicking and wasting time troubleshooting why your brand-new GPU isn't being recognised either.
Note: I am a bit of an idiot when it comes to building PCs, so I'm sure most of the people out there won't struggle the way I did, but I sure did and hope that this review will help at least one other person.

As for the product itself- it works as advertised. Not a man of many words, unfortunately. It fits my 14th Gen CPU and I can easily control the RGB on my fans, which I've learned has a practical use of quickly telling if your parts are functioning at a glance. Motherboard itself is sturdy and doesn't feel cheaply built, and upon booting my PC properly the first time, a little menu popped up with a list of drivers that I could install/update without having to go look for them individually- though I had already downloaded all of them prior to taking apart my PC.

Overall, the MSI B550 Gaming GEN3 is a solid and reliable motherboard that offers great performance for the price. It’s ideal for a mid-range gaming build or any Ryzen-based system where you don’t need PCIe 4.0. Highly recommended for its balance of features and value.

### **MSI B550 Gaming Gen3 Motherboard Review**

The **MSI B550 Gaming Gen3 Motherboard** strikes a solid balance between performance, features, and value. Aimed at gamers and PC builders looking for a mid-range motherboard, it offers a feature-packed design with excellent support for Ryzen processors and next-gen connectivity.

The B550 Gaming Gen3 is well-equipped when it comes to I/O options. It features **USB 3.2 Gen 2** ports, as well as **USB Type-C** for modern devices, making it a versatile board for peripherals. #### **Final Thoughts**
For gamers, content creators, and enthusiasts looking for a reliable and cost-effective motherboard, the **MSI B550 Gaming Gen3** is an excellent choice. I originally had an ASUS B350 board before this, but I had to return it since it wouldn't POST with my Ryzen 7 3700X without a BIOS update. Since the ASUS customer support was a joke, and AMD's RMA form was down, I got this MSI board for the replacement. While it doesn't have as much features as the ASUS board for the same money, it was compatible with my CPU right out of the box. (Make sure you get the MSI boards with "MAX" in the title, as those come pre-installed with the BIOS update for 3rd gen Ryzen.)

As for features, it's pretty basic. However for someone like me, who is coming from a used Dell business machine with a Core i5 2500 and no USB 3, it's still a substantial upgrade. The board has an aesthetic that will put you to sleep, though it's not like I'm going to stare at the damn thing while I work. It does have a 12V RGBW, so if you're into that sort of thing, at least you're covered.

One thing that I actually liked about the board was the ability to adjust the fan curve in the UEFI. At first, when I installed my CPU, the fan would ramp up and down jarringly at idle, and it was pretty annoying. Thankfully, I was able to adjust the fan curve pretty easily in the motherboard UEFI. For the most part, the problem went away.

Overall, this is a solid board so far. If you're in my camp, and you just want a cheap motherboard that works with 3rd Gen Ryzen out of the box, then you should consider this board.

text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
I picked this board for a basic budget build. I needed something reliable for a 12th gen Intel CPU, and this was one of the more affordable options with decent reviews. I wasn’t trying to overclock or run a GPU-heavy setup, just something stable for a home workstation.
Board quality:
The board feels solid for the price point. No flexing, no janky connectors. All the standoffs lined up properly in a standard mATX case, and nothing felt cheap or fragile during install. The VRMs aren’t designed for heavy loads but they’re fine for non-gaming purposes.
Value for money:
You get what you pay for here. It’s a no-frills board with just the essentials, which is what I wanted. If you’re building something basic like a home office PC or even a light-duty media rig, this gets the job done without blowing your budget. It supports DDR4 which helped me save by reusing existing RAM.
Looks:
Plain and neutral. No RGB, no heatsinks with logos, just a black-and-gray aesthetic that blends in. Perfect if you don’t care about case windows or flashy setups. Personally, I liked that it doesn’t draw attention.
Functionality:
It does the basics right. Boots quickly, no BIOS issues out of the box. Recognized CPU and RAM on first power-on. No problems with USB ports or LAN. You only get two RAM slots, and limited fan headers, so this isn’t for expanding later. But if you know your needs are modest, it’s totally fine.
Boot speed:
System boots fast with a Gen3 NVMe SSD. BIOS loads quickly too. No lag or delays after POST. Not the fastest board out there, but definitely not slow either.
Port capacity:
Pretty minimal. Only a couple of SATA ports and no USB-C. Rear I/O is basic, and internal headers are limited. But again, for a budget setup with a single drive and one or two peripherals, it covers the essentials.

Overall, good for stripped-down, reliable systems that don’t need flashy extras or tons of ports. Stable, efficient, and straightforward.

I purchased the B450 Gaming Plus ATX motherboard for my recent budget build. The motherboard came is an attractive and secure box with all the hardware required for installation. Note that I purchased the ATX version so I did not have any issues with CPU cooler installation like others have stated with the mAtx boards. As you can see in the pictures, I have a fairly large cooler attached to the board without issue or interference from neighboring components (Ignore the cable routing, was not done routing when this picture was taken).

This board states it is compatible with Ryzen 3 series CPU's out of the box, I can verify this as my Ryzen 5 3600 booted up without issue and no driver updates were needed. The locations for the ports on the board are fairly well thought out, the only thing I would like to see is more fan headers but luckily my cooling fans also had a plug to directly wire to the power supply. Downside to this is you lose fan control but that is not an issue for me as my fans are static rpm.

Cons:

The bios boot time for this board is extremely slow. I would guess about 10-15 seconds for the board to post and boot the computer. While not a deal breaker it is definitely an annoyance. Good news is that MSI has addressed this and released an updated firmware that resolves this issue.

I would recommend this motherboard for budget builds or PC builders that do not care for all the flashy RGB and RGB controller components. This has been installed for over three months of daily use and I have not had one issue with this motherboard.

text:
This is the second MSI motherboard I've used (previously an FM2-A75MA-E35 that still works flawlessly 7 years later). Once again, MSI has nailed it.

Installation was a breeze and the board is well-labeled. The manual is consice and easy to follow. For me, this board was very nearly plug and play. The BIOS is user friendly and similar in design to my old FM2 board (meaning they got a good design years ago and have only needed to make minor changes) which made this upgrade significantly easier. Using the MSI Live Update tool made updating drivers quick and simple. I have not had to use them in anger but the EZ Debug LEDs are a great troubleshooting feature.

This board has 4 case fan plugs which is a major step up from my old board's 1 case fan plug (this resulted in me removing my old front panel fan controller and savings tons of wiring headache). Setting the fan schedules in BIOS was intuitive and provided a few options for fan management. The one downside was using MSI Command Center for fan management; the profiles never seemed to remain after a reboot. This was easily fixed setting the values within the BIOS instead.

The SATA ports are located in a manner such that they can all be used. My old FM2 board would have at least two ports blocked with a moderately sized graphics card. With this board, no issues. I don't yet have an m.2 drive so I can't comment on that.

Some other reviews have mentioned issues with other components fitting (e.g. RAM or case fans) but I've had no issues in a HAF 912 with a 200mm top exhaust fan and a 120mm rear exhaust fan. The AMD cooler fits perfectly with no interference.

Overall, I'm extremely pleased with this board.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros:
- Decent price, about $75 when I bought it.
- Good build quality. I didn't have any issues with it when assembling the PC.
- Built-in memory profiles. I can't speak for all the possible memory types out there, but I paired it with the reasonably-priced Patriot Viper 4 Series Extreme Performance DDR4 16GB (2 X 8GB) 3200MHz Kit (PC4-25600) and I didn't have to do anything special or create custom settings. I selected the first of the built-in enhanced profiles and restarted the system; the next time I went into the BIOS the memory was running at the rated speed.
- BIOS and on-board HDMI port worked great with the AMD Ryzen 5 3400G chip with integrated Vega graphics. No special updating necessary on the version of the board I got. It was all plug-and-play except for switching to the first enhanced memory profile.

Cons:
- One of my older mobos can sort of update the BIOS itself (from within the BIOS UI you can tell it to update and if it has network connectivity, it can do it on its own). With this one I had to use the utility app in Windows to download it. Not much of a con, but after the other board's convenience I had thought more would have the same features.
- If you need a lot of expansion capacity, you will want a different board. This has two memory banks and not many expansion slots; understandable because of the micro-ATX format, but just something to be aware of.

I thought it was a very good board overall. Plenty of power and features for the budget PC I built around it. The only quirk was that I had to buy a splitter cable for the fans. The mobo has a CPU fan connector and one other fan connector. I needed the splitter since the case had two fans.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text: I was a bit hesitant to purchase this board after reading many reviews and watching Tech Yes City’s review on youtube. It seems that early bios revisions for this board had major compatibility issues with certain Ryzen cpus and only worked with certain brands of ram. Thankfully, my Ryzen 7500F and Teamgroup Elite DDR5 5600 Ram POST’d without issue. Memory training did not take long and before long I was able to get into bios. The only changes I made were to set a more conservative cpu fan curve so that the fan would reach 100% when the cpu got to 60C and to set ram speed to 5600mhz to match my ram. The system would not boot into windows with these settings, which was disappointing. Ive seen MSI advertise this board as compatible with Ram up to 6000mhz, but for me 5200mhz was all I could do. I made the decision to use AMD’s wraith stealth cooler because Tech Yes City’s review of the MSI A620m showed that a down draft cpu cooler kept the vrm temperatures low and made up for a lack of vrm heatsinks which are standard on more expensive motherboards. Sadly the little AMD Wraith Stealth is not enough to cool even the 7500F, which is the lowest end cpu on the AM5 platform. I did not even run cinebench, just tried a couple games. Cyberpunk 2077 with high crowds and a 60fps cap pushed the temp of the 7500F into the mid 80sC, and this was only like a 50% load. So this means I will be switching to a better tower cooler for the CPU which will not blow air directly over the VRM. To make up for this, I bought stick on vrm heatsinks on Amazon for $7. So cost of the motherboard is realistically $82 for me now, as I don’t think it would be wise to run it without heatsinks with a tower cooler as in Tech Yes City’s testing, the VRM temps were reaching 90C. Because of these high temps, MSI limits the power output of this board to 90 watts, so you should not pair this board with anything except a 7500F, 7600, or 8400F. Any CPU that draws over 90 watts will be bottlenecked by this board and limited to just 90 watts. Keep in mind though, the 8400F is a newer CPU and reviews are still stating this board is shipping with a bios too old to boot with the 8400F. So as of this moment, the 7500F and 7600 are the only CPUs I can be certain are compatible. In conclusion, this board is a great budget option as long as you work within its limitations. Pair it with a budget AM5 cpu, and if you use anything other than a down draft cpu cooler, buy some cheap stick on vrm heatsinks just to be safe. The board may be able to operate at those high temperatures, but I am sure it will live a longer life if you can keep everything running cooler.

These MSI EZ120 fans are genuinely a game-changer for building a clean PC. text:
This laptop is a solid machine for gaming, image editing, and for having hundreds of tabs open like the monster I am. What got me to write this review, though, is that this laptop is built to last.

I'll admit, I'm rough on my machines. I take my laptop into the woods on camping trips, throw that sucker into my backpack without thought for what else is in there, and chuck it into the backseat of my car without regard for where it lands. The MSI Stealth's metal body appealed to me, and it was doing great with my rough handling.

Then I managed to set my (black) laptop down on the hood of my (black) car, and drive away. The laptop impacted the ground going almost 45 miles an hour, which as you may imagine, isn't great for laptops. I expected a total loss. The right screen hinge was snapped off. The screen and keyboard were warped. The back right corner of the computer was bent at a 45-degree angle.

When I got home, I crossed my fingers, held my breath, and booted it up.

The laptop booted just fine. There were no damaged pixels on the screen, the keyboard worked flawlessly, and because the fans aren't all linked together, only the one bent fan failed to run. I lost no data, was able to prep for my conference, and the only annoyance was that the screen didn't stand up well with only one hinge. Honestly, I was amazed.

If you need a reliable laptop that can stand up to your active lifestyle, this is the machine for you. I already loved MSI - now they have a customer for life.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
REASON FOR PURCHASE - I purchased this laptop because my Dell XPS 8100 desktop kept freezing/restarting several times a day. A fresh clean re-install of Windows 10 was not remedying the situation, and I had no desire to troubleshoot every component to see what was the underlying problem. Overall, this issue was seriously affecting my productivity, as well as sanity.

POTENTIAL ALTERNATIVES - I was mainly looking for a desktop replacement - not a laptop. I checked Dell, Amazon, BestBuy, as well as other 'PC build' websites such as 'ibuypower', but found prices too high overall. Basically, the price was the driving factor for me in purchasing this laptop. The final price was slightly under $1,300 w/ taxes, and I found that to be a fair price for performance ratio.

MUST HAVES - Since this was my first PC replacement in nearly 10-years, I wanted to make sure I got a 11th Gen i7 Intel processor, as well as an RTX 3000 series graphics card. I was looking for a RTX 3060ti minimum, but I could not find a match within my budget.

PREVIOUS HARDWARE - My Dell XPS 8100 was still using the 1st Gen i5 650 processor, with a PNY GTX 970 updated graphics card. I honestly would have gone another year or two before changing my PC, if these freezing problems were not there.

FIRST IMPRESSIONS - Seems well built - I also liked the keyboard lighting. Chassis seems solid, and I liked all the available ports on the sides. The design was appealing, being perfectly rectangle with the lid closed - no protruding sections to put the shape out of balance.

HOW IT IS USED - I use this laptop as a desktop replacement - I only open the screen lid to power it on. Otherwise, I use an external monitor and keyboard.

HOW OFTEN USED - I keep this laptop on for at least 8-hours a day. It was purchased roughly a month ago, so it's been used rather frequently.

GAMING (@ 1080p only) - It is a notable upgrade from my Dell. Previously in games like WoW or FFXIV, I was getting under 60 FPS frequently in crowded areas. Now, I get dizzy by how quickly the screen rotates in-game, forcing me to lower the mouse-sensitivity. In WoW, I am constantly at 100 FPS with the occasional dips to 90 FPS. I'm also currently playing Ubisoft's 'The Division', but the max I can get is 60 FPS with regular dips to 47 FPS @ medium settings. Not killer performance, but a huge upgrade nevertheless.

FAN NOISE - For everyday non-gaming use (i.e., web browsing), it is a low hum you can only hear if you're within 20-inches to the laptop. When gaming, it can ramp up to a constant loud whirl.

HEAT - Similarly to fan noise, heat is negligible for non-gaming use. For gaming, it can get warm over time, but I use this product: 'Zimilar Monitor Stand Riser', to keep it propped up for heat dissipation. It seems to work well in keeping this laptop cool.

STORAGE - It only comes with one 512GB M.2 device, so storage for my gaming needs is very limited. I looked at YouTube videos to see if it can be upgraded, but it honestly looked like a PITA to do so. So, I have invested in external SSD solutions for space.

WIFI – My router is roughly 25-feet away (through walls), but I get consistent download/upload speeds with the occasional dip. No major connection loss or issues otherwise.

BLOATWARE - It comes with a lot of MSi propriety software, as well as Norton Security Suite. Also, a trial version of Microsoft Office 365. I spent a good amount of time sorting through, and uninstalling a lot of them.

BATTERY - I've only tested it off the plug once. Even without gaming, it was eating through the battery pretty quickly. I surmise it'd only go about 3-hours before draining out. This laptop is definitely not recommended if longevity off the plug is a priority of yours.

PROBLEMS – The only ‘issue’ I’ve come across is if I’ve gamed for a long period of time, or I’ve been moving large files around. The performance of the laptop may drop significantly. I remedy this by a simple reboot, which clears up the issue. Also to note, this laptop has not frozen on me once.

CONCLUSION - When I purchased this laptop, I considered it an intermediary, until I gathered the necessary funds to invest in a desktop with a minimum of RTX 3070. However, it has proven to be a mini-powerhouse. I don't play above 1080p, and I can live with medium-settings if performance seems to dip. It performs excellently on non-gaming tasks, and I now have a mobile gaming platform if I want to take it to a friend's house. All-in-all, I am quite satisfied with my purchase, and may now wait until the RTX 4000 series come out before I consider a desktop.

Overall, highly recommended for purchase.
--------------------------------------------------

UPDATE 08/28/2022

CURRENT STATUS - Yes, it's still working fine. Performance has not dipped, and I only re-installed Windows 11 once because I replaced the 512GB M.2 with a 'Samsung 970 EVO 2TB' several months ago. Also, despite being on 8-hours a day or more, the keyboard LEDs are still functioning bright. That's more than 2,900-hours that this laptop has been on since its purchase.

HARDWARE ISSUES - None. Screen, ports, fans, WiFi, Bluetooth, and trackpad are all still working fine - of course given the caveat that I still strictly use an external keyboard/mouse/monitor setup.

NEW REVELATIONS - Only one. Gaming off the AC Adaptor is a fool's errand. Performance throttled severely after 10-minutes because the laptop was getting so hot, and the battery lasted no more than 35-minutes tops. This was while playing 'Aliens: Fireteam' on Steam.

PRODUCT OVERVIEW - I am still happy with my purchase and see no need to change for several more years. Of course, if I find myself with a lot of disposable income, I can see myself getting a new gaming desktop. But beyond that scenario, I am perfectly content with its performance and durability.

text:
I had a prior build since early 2020, with an Antec PSU that shorted out recently and died with a bang, and in the process killed the motherboard (MSI). Fortunately, my M.2 NVMe Intel disc (with Windows 11 Pro) was intact, and I did not know then about the CPU (Ryzen 5 3400G Picasso) or RAM (16GB Crucial Ballistix 8GBx2). Typically, a PSU outputs first to the MOBO and CPU, and next to the RAM. Older memories were notoriously susceptible to current and used to die with the MOBO. Fortunately, things have gotten better. Antec was great in sending me a new replacement PSU under warranty. I needed a new replacement MOBO and wanted to stick with AM4 chipset without spending a lot. I found this board on Amazon at a great price, and the several positive reviews were encouraging. Throughout the years, I had always used MSI boards for my builds, except once (ASUS). This was my first experience with ASRock, and I am very pleased so far. The box I received states "AMD Ryzen Desktop 2000 Ready" and had an added sticker "AMD Ryzen 5000 Desktop Ready", and another "Windows 11 Ready". I imagine some (older) stock did not have the added (Ryzen 5000) sticker, which would explain some reviewers who had to update the Bios using an earlier generation CPU. When I received it, I did a minimal basic build outside the case, with the new PSU and tested my old CPU and RAM. It booted into BIOS and I was so relieved that the CPU and RAM were fine. I then put the Intel NVMe disc, placed the board in the case, hooked my old Plextor DVDRW, case fans and all the headers. Windows 11 Pro loaded up and all is good. The Bios/set up on this ASRock board is very easy to navigate and has a lot of 'AUTO' settings in the default parameters, and I only had to change few things. For the technically savvy, there are several settings you can adjust, but for most people, you will only need the boot menu, particularly for Win 11, and very few advanced configurations. I did not even use the included support CD. The box contains the MOBO, CD, Installation guide, 2 SATA cables, a small M.2 screw and the I/O shield. The guide and illustrations are very adequate. It has 2 DIMM slots (288 pin) and supports up to 64GB, 32GBx2, per ASRock. I bought new 32GB RAM (16GBx2) which was easily recognized. ASRock states for Picasso, the frequency is 2667/2933, but the new memory is 3200 and runs as such, with or without XMP. I am not a gamer and never overclock a CPU and don't use a discrete GPU anymore. It has on board USB2 (x2) and USB3 headers. The CPU connector is only 4 pin and if you have an 8-pin cable (4+4), you just split it. The MOBO is the standard 24 pin. There are 2 chassis fan connectors (4 pin and 3 pin), 4 SATA connectors, HD audio and a standard front panel system header. There is one M.2 and 2 PCI slots. The I/O shield is as shown (Single PS2, but supports Y-splitter, 2 USB2, 4 USB3, Gigabit LAN, rear audio, VGA, DVI and HDMI). It is a basic board (No WIFI, BT, M-Flash, USB C) and is very well priced. As such, I would recommend as a budget motherboard. Even though I am biased toward MSI boards (I guess force of habit), I will definitely keep this motherboard in mind. Thank you.

I bought a second one to upgrade an older computer (Athlon A6 APU and FM2+ socket MOBO). It also had the Ryzen 5000 and Windows 11 ready stickers. Very satisfied, just like the first time. Recommend. Thank you.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
For the price (normally in the $60 range) it is difficult to find a better value Currently shipping product supports Ryzen 3000 series out of the box. Review sites rate the AsRock B450 motherboards well (in the budget category)

Everything went together well, the board's compact size made it easy to slide into my existing computer case without removing other components. Fired right up.

The board comes with overclocking menus and abilities in BIOS. But I wouldn't bother. Unlike most boards that allow overclocking, this one has no "failure to boot" reset feature. If you make an OC change in BIOS that prevents boot up, then you are going to have to use the CMOS jumper on the motherboard to clear it. Made worse is that the slot for the video card is right on the edge of the motherboard. It's impossible to get to the clear CMOS jumper without removing the video card if using a smaller case (which most people would be using if wanting a micro ATX motherboard) And the SATA motherboard connectors are also right in line with the video card. So if you use a full size video card, the only way to get to the SATA connectors (say if one comes loose or you add another drive) is to pull the video card.

The motherboard also only has two memory slots. That really shouldn't count as too much the negative. Just be aware and order the amount of memory you want - with two sticks - up front. For an extra $15 ASRock makes the B450 Pro4 motherboard that has four memory slots and two video card slots, one further located further up from the edge of the board so the video card out of the way of way of CMOS jumper. Looks like a full size video card would still hang over the SATA connectors though.

If I had to do it over again, I'd still buy this board. Price is right and I didn't plan on overclocking anyway. MSI makes a similar board at the same price. But reviews here indicate a higher DOA rate with the MSI board.

text:
It depends on what you need a new laptop for. If you're looking for maximal mobility and a long battery life, this isn't going to do it for you. If you're looking for a decent gaming/work studio appliance, look no further. "Decent" might be underselling it. For well under $1,000 you're getting an adequate gaming computer that will run any new title you throw at it to some extent, usually a high and satisfying extent. The GPU and CPU will offer all the power you need whether it's for video editing or watching high definition movies. There should be scarce to no hiccups with your product, as there barely is any with the laptop I received. I have to admit MSI is a good brand with a reputation for quality they actually bother to maintain. I'll give you my pros an cons for the MSI GF63 I received.

PROS: The GPU and CPU are powerful. No individual editing, gaming, or audio mixing software program will suffer too many hiccups. After one week, I haven't dealt with any crashes at all what so ever, and I have been stressing it with some pretty intense gaming and video editing. Minor lagging here and there but not an obstacle. The audio is decent by the way. The build is sturdy -- there shouldn't be any cosmetic issues with regular use. Obviously you'll want to avoid dropping it. The screen casing is metallic and thin, the rest is a hard, somewhat jagged (though not uncomfortable) sturdy plastic. The keyboard has a red back-light with three levels of brightness. You get an anti-glare display with clean 1080p definition, though it is yellow-shifted by default. You can easily fix that and get a more balanced color scheme out of it. Other notes about this model in case there is any confusion: it should come with 3 USB 3.0 slots, an HDMI in the back, a mic jack, a headphone jack, an ethernet port, and a micro USB type C port.

CONS: The mousepad sucks. Buy a mouse, even the cheapest ones are an improvement. This mousepad is a single wobbly plastic platform of pure crap. The keyboard, though comfortable to type on, does not come with a number pad. If you absolutely need one then you should just buy this laptop anyway, you're getting a good deal. You'll have saved plenty to purchase any extensions you need. The battery life isn't amazing. If you're gaming you'll want to charge it every couple of hours or so. For mundane web surfing, light gaming, and photo editing, the battery will last 4hrs or so, a decent bump of entertainment if you're taking a flight. The SSD is quick, but meek. At 250GB, you should already expect to need an external HDD for serious storage. You'll have to have the fan's highest settings enabled to run intense graphics, which will be somewhat loud. Personally I don't care, if the audio means so much to you then you should have a decent set of headphones anyway. Most importantly, this isn't a highly mobile rig. Expect to have an external HDD or other extensions dangling off of it a lot of the time. If you're taking it camping, expect to have an ample battery bank.

CONCLUSION: If you station this laptop upon your desk it shall be a fantastic and leisurely delight to use. Don't expect great mobility. If you want a failry smooth and responsive computer for a good deal, then stop looking around because you've really found it. If my experience continues to be as positive as it is, then you will not hear from me again, otherwise I will keep you updated.

Update: After two weeks this laptop is still performing flawlessly and I am pleased. Been gaming nonstop. Out of the 6 laptops I've been through this one is best.

- Red backlighting isn't overly bright, and i believe you can dim it more. I just never had the need to.
-500gb storage is mainly for windows items and updates. the mini C connector i use for an external storage that has no delay or lag at all for my steam games. otherwise it's more than enough for the school and classes i'm taking
-audio is crisp and adjustable. no real scratchy isms unless I'm just being an idiot and watching troll ASMR videos to spite my co inhabitants lol

The Cons
- unless your running the cooler boost setting in the dragon center your top left of the laptop will get hot real quick. That graphics card pushes itself to perform up to par with gaming you throw at it and if you put your hands up that way you'll feel it real quick. I'd imagine that along with the cooler boost setting and a laptop fan dock it'd be a bit less toasty but you'll notice the temp (and the NOISE) once it's rising.
- 500gb storage for people who want more than 10 games. you gotta consider that with onboard storage windows itself will eventually take up 50gb+ of space and it's always advisable to have 50gb of free storage you'll never really use 'cept for real emergencies. this means you have roughly 400gb or less of actual storage space to use. You can get a small form external storage for pretty cheap at 1TB otherwise
- The charge isn't much. I think on low battery usage, very light gaming and dimming down the backscreen I managed about 5 maybe 6 hours. That's a deal breaker for those who tend to be more mobile than the standard gamer
- any time, and i mean ANY time you run an update your fan will speed up. windows update? fans rev up. graphics card update? fans definitely rev up. if you're in a quiet place I'd consider holding off on updates lol
- no side number pad. for the screen size this is to be expected but if you've never gone less than standard screen size like this you're in for a real adjustment period.
-EDGES ON YOUR WRISTS.

Aside from those Pros and Cons the system starts up right away. boot to windows in roughly 5-7 seconds and programs on the internal SSD start up on access quick. It has been a great purchase for what i game with and how i game, as well as holding all my school stuff without error. It seems like a majority of the erroneous reviews are because they went with the 1050 graphics card (at this point in time anything less than a 1080 6gb minimum will give you issues to be honest). the price difference was only like $100 when i compared both.

text:
This processor is a beast, it can handle most task thrown at it. It is a 3 module, 2 core per module so 6 core CPU with 1.2 billion transistors. Despite being technology from 2012, they are still in production and mine was 2017 made. This CPU is black edition CPU meaning you can easily overclock or even underclock it using unlocked multiplier in BIOS.

It also has the latest instruction set like SSE 4.1, SSE 4.2, AVX etc. when this CPU was introduced it was for high end PCs, but now despite being 2012 technology this CPU still rocks and rivals many latest low (celeron, pentium, i3) to mid range (i5) CPUs and even beats older generation i7. This CPU easily beats the popular Pentium G4560 in performance.

If you have a AM3+ motherboard and dont want to fully upgrade your PC then upgrading to this CPU is better choice then going to other AM3 socket phenom or athlon CPU which lacks instruction set like SSE4.2. latest CPU dont support Windows 7, only windows 10, so if you want to use Windows 7 and dont want to fully upgrade your PC, then this is best choice. Earlier I had a Athlon x260 and after upgrading I can see major performance improvement. If you want to use this CPU then visit the motherboard manufacture website to see the list of compatible CPUs, I have a Asus AM3+ motherboard. AM3+ is backward compatible with AM3 so there is high chances of you motherboard supporting both.

The only problem with this CPU is that it overheats, this is due to high TDP of 95W & AMD Turbo Core technology which automatically overclocks the CPU giving 300mhz extra when needed, the max of this CPU is 3.5Ghz, under turbo core (boost) the speed goes upto 3.8Ghz, This causes heat. So to avoid overheating issue, its best to turn off turbo core feature in your BIOS. In winter time the CPU temperature remains cool about 10-12C on idle and 20-30C on loads like web browsing, watching video. I am using the stock heatsink and cooler and they are working fine, and I have disabled the turbo core.

If you are getting a FX then get a CPU modal with 2nd number 3, like 4300, 6300. 2nd number 3 are the piledriver version of FX, which is a minor upgrade over the original FX codenamed bulldozer.

I purchased this from Amazon global store for Rs. 4000 + Rs 1880 duty + Rs. 480 shipping, it cost me around Rs. 6400. if you can get this for under 6-7k then its a good deal, else look FX 4300 or get used CPU which are available under 3k.

text:
Got this fan installed yesterday!
Upon close inspection I noticed that the blades of the fan were a TINY bit thicker - which matters a LOT as these fans are razor thin! I estimate these to be .1 to .2mm longer in the blades than stock than the last set I had - which means more airflow!

And it only gets better! Not ONLY do these fans (both CPU and GPU as sold by Quetterlee) go FAST! My CPU fan maxes out around 5900 RPM - which is EXACTLY what they should do - and the GPU fans max out around 5200 RPM - which is also - what the stock fans do!

But then I noticed, these fans are QUIETER AS WELL! My last set at max speed made an almost ear piercingly loud whistle - these are FAR quieter at any given RPM - Max is basically as loud as my last set at ~75%! And there is NO LOUD WHISTLING!

By far the best replacements I have found anywhere, and these are DEFINITELY the best quality I have seen!

I will be dilligently cleaning my laptop out as usual, and I will let you guys know if I have ANY sort of issue down the road. If they die on me 3+ years down the track - I will still say that is a decent product, but I am hoping for longer with compressed air and small picks to stop the fans from spinning (if you blast air and spin fans too fast you can break them) - I will revisit and revise my review as needed, but I doubt highly I will need to change anything said so far!

I bought an entire set from another seller - and the CPU fan maxed out at a measly ~3800 RPM - the GPU at just ~3500 - this is NOT enough to cool a GS63VR 6RF while gaming! The last seller did, however care about my complaints and sent me a second set free of charge - and I WANTED to like them, but same issue... And I see that in a LOT of other brand's reviews for these fans!

text:
Acheté pour faire une nouvelle config pour remplacer mon ancien boitier qui était une NZXT Noctis 450.
Pour une idée de la config installé dedans j'ai un i5-10600k, RTX 2070 super windforce de chez Gigabyte, watercooling MSI mag coreliquid 240r ca va vous donnez une ordre d'idée des performances qu'on peut installé dedans et du refroidissement qui suivra.
Niveau taille le boitier est clairement petit comparer a mon ancien pour vous dire je peux clairement faire rentrer le carton du MSI dans le carton du NZXT. Une fois la config installé dedans ca fait un pc très compacte, il y a de la place que pour le nécessaire mais ca ne bloque pas les possibilité possible malgré ca.
Niveau design il est vraiment très quali, bande ARGB et logo ARGB sur la façade avant, verre trempé sur le coté vraiment très beau aussi, le design de l'aération sur le dessus est propre est bien optimisé pour le passage de l'air. Et le petit plus c'est qu'il est vendu directement avec les 3 ventilateurs en façade ARGB et le ventilateur arrière ARGB aussi.
Niveau montage de la config dedans c'est très simple et clair je trouve, le système de fixation des panneaux latéraux est très bien pensé car il suffit juste de retiré les 2 vis qui tienne le panneaux du dessus qu'on glisse vers l'arrière et les 2 panneaux latéraux on juste a être glissé vers le haut pour les enlevés, même pas besoin de vis c'est très pratique.
Niveau refroidissement il est aussi très bien équipé avec ses filtres mesh en façade, sur le dessus et sous l'alimentation ce qui rend le nettoyage très simple et rapide a faire plus tard.
Niveau bruit le boitier par contre est un peu bruyant si on cherche a gardé ces composants au frais ( maxi 40/45° pour mon processeur et 65/70° pour la carte graphique) et ceci est dû uniquement a la conception du boitier car c'est un boitier fermé avec les entrées d'air uniquement a l'avant sur les cotés de la façade ce qu'il fait des entrées d'air d'uniquement 2/3cm de chaque coté ce qui favorise pas le silence si on veut les performances de refroidissement.

Conclusion : excellent boitier je ne suis pas déçu pour le prix il est vraiment bien fourni et permet de faire de belle config dedans et encore mieux quand on prend tout MSI comme ca on synchronise tout le RGB et ca permet de très beau rendu final.

text:
Esse gabinete é um grande avanço comparado com o gabinete anterior que eu tinha e aqui destaco os 5 pontos positivos e 2 negativos:
1 - Primeiramente ele vem com uma porta USB-C 3.2, com transferência de até 20Gbps. É fato que o USB-C se popularizou, porém gabinetes que vem com conector USB-C com grandes taxas de transferência ainda são raros e os poucos gabinetes que vem tem uma porta USB-C 3.1, com velocidades de até 10Gbps.

2 - Os cabos do painel frontal são unificados, isso significa que não tem risco de conectar os cabos do HDD LED, POWER LED, POWER SW etc errados pois eles já vem em um único encaixe montado para ser conectado na placa mãe. Essa foi a maior vantagem que eu vi.

3 - Esse gabinete possui diversas aberturas para passagem de cabos. Entretanto, ao invés de aberturas de metal que contorcem (e às vezes até danifica), as aberturas desse gabinete da MSI utilizam uma espécie de plástico que "suaviza" essa passagem de cabos. De forma resumida, há menos riscos do cabo de alimentação da placa mãe ser contorcido desnecessariamente.

4 - Esse gabinete possui um controle RGB integrado. Basta conectar os cabos das ventoinhas RGB que ele gerencia as cores sozinho, sem precisar do software MSI Center instalado no PC.

5 - Esse gabinete vem com 4 ventoinhas RGB pré-instaladas, não sendo necessário comprar à parte.

6 - Esse gabinete vem com manual de instruções muito fraco. Uma pessoa leiga não irá saber montar corretamente, pois ele vem apenas com imagens ilustrativas. Não há passo a passo de montagem e tampouco o tipo de parafuso a ser utilizado.

7 - A tampa é de vidro temperado, que é consideravelmente mais pesada que o acrílico. Tem que tomar cuidado ao manusear a tampa do gabinete.

Uma dica importante: o cabo do controlador que vem na parte lateral direta deve ser conectado no conector JRAINBOW da placa-mãe, jamais conecte no conector SYSTEMFAN ou poderá queimar todas as ventoinhas

I'm rarely inclined to leave a product review. However, based on my experience with this product and ALSEYE, I feel so inclined.

I bought this air cooler because of the digital display, the size of the cooler, and other reviews (you know, the ones I rarely leave). Upon receiving my item, I instantly set it up. I followed the instructions to download the BEM software needed to allow the cooler to read the temperature of the CPU, but I kept getting an error message on the ALSEYE website regarding a 502 Gateway Error.
I reached out to ALSEYE, told them of my dilemma, and they messaged me back with rapidity. Their message contained several apologies, and they told me to take a photograph of my email address and send them the photograph. I did that, and ALSEYE emailed me a zippered folder containing the direct link to the BEM software. OUTSTANDING!

I couldn't be happier with my purchase. The cooler keeps my CPU nice and cool, and the RGB's work flawlessly (though, I'll admit I rarely, RARELY use the RGB feature).

NOTE: In order for the cooler to show your CPU's temperature, you have to double-click on the software icon on your desktop every time you use it. Otherwise, it only shows 24C. I have not found a way to have the cooler's display "remember" to show the actual temperature when I turn on my system. But that's not a problem for me as it takes two seconds.
NOTE: The cooler's display shows the CPU's temperature to within five degrees, give or take, of the actual degree. The cooler display will show 38 degrees C, while NZXT Cam shows 34 degrees C, while AMD Adrenalin shows 36 degrees C. Which one is correct is beyond me. But I'm not complaining, only stating my observation and sharing with potential buyers of this awesome product.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I may be dating myself here, but my first computer that I booted to an a: prompt was an IBM 8088 clone. It might have had 32k of ram, if memory serves. I can't begin to recount how many cpu coolers I've used, but I've owned very name brand you can think of, and some pretty legendary air and water coolers, such as the Thermalright Silver Arrow, and the Corsair H150i AIW water cooler (which is currently on my i7 12700k). And probably another 20 or 30 in there somewhere. Maybe 40, lol. The point is, you would be hard pressed to find someone who's had more CPU coolers pass through their hands in the last 40 years.

Though I haven't yet installed this on the intended recipient (an Asus-equipped i7 13700k w/ 64gb DDR5) and run any actual testing, I have taken it out of the box and given it a very serious inspection. Point blank, as someone who has used the best names in the business, my initial impression of this CPU cooler is, frankly, WOW.

To start with, the build quality is equal or better to anything I've ever seen or used. If this was some cheap, hacked-together Chinese junk, I'd be the absolute first in line to tell you "run away". But, instead, I'm the first to tell you this is an air cooler you should seriously consider if you're building an air-cooled system.

I'd like to especially mention the cpu interface place (the part that actually touches the CPU and draws heat away). I have seen some very rough CPU plates in my day, and I have in fact spent many hours and hours with a CPU cooler, some wet-or-dry sandpaper, a piece of glass, and a lot of back and forth sanding of many CPU coolers to make the flat and smooth. I can't begin to tell you the number of CPU coolers I've lapped, but I've been doing it since the socket A days. There aren't many CPU interface plates I've looked at, that I can honestly say, nah, I wouldn't even bother lapping it because the machine work is already nearly flawless.

I can honestly say, the machine work on this CPU plate is perhaps close to the best, if not THE best I've ever seen. It is smooth beyond smooth, and the grooves in the surface are so fine, it appears more like a CD / DVD surface, with a "rainbow effect" as you tilt it in the light. I've seen a lot of CPU coolers, so for me to say this is close the best, if not THE best machine work I've ever seen, is quite the statement.

And, thankfully, it does NOT come with any pre-applied thermal interface material. Trust me, every computer builder worth their stuff uses a high-quality thermal interface material (TIM) and cleans off the pre-applied gunk anyway. So, as someone that considers themselves a "serious computer builder", I'm quite tickled that they didn't bother pre-applying a TIM that I was going to wipe off anyway. All CPU cooler manufacturers should follow suit, here. If you were to ask me, "What should I use?", I recommend using Google for "Best CPU paste" and make your own choice. I definitely don't want to wade into a "CPU paste" debate for the purpose of this review, just know that 1, you have to supply your own, and 2, that's a good thing.

While I didn't install this on my Asus motherboard yet, I did plug it into my currently running system to listen to the noise output and check the airflow. I found at the high end of the spectrum, it moved a very good amount of air, while being a bit noisy, though certainly not the noisiest I've ever used. At the lower end of things, it was near silent, easily being overshadowed by my power supply fan.

And, speaking of the fans themselves, herein lies the reason for my -1 star rating. Because, otherwise, this cooler deserves 5 stars, and I haven't even put it on a board yet. I'm that confident it will perform well from what I've so far seen and from a lot of experience. But my only complaint, is about the front fan. It's a SPECIAL fan. If the front (they call it a "Koala" fan...for a reason I'm not yet sure of) fan ever fails...and they all do in time...there simply is no replacing it, unless they still happen to be selling them. Good luck.

Now, how terrible is this, really? Well, for one thing, the fans it comes equipped with are double ball bearing fans. In the "IT" world, we have a saying about fans...there are 2 types, double ball bearing fans, and NOT double ball bearing fans. You'll see all kinds of jibberish fans..."magnetic levitation bearings"..."fluid dynamic bearings"...blah blah blah. What those all mean, are that they are NOT double ball bearing fans. In no uncertain terms, the double ball bearing fan WILL outlast everything else, hands down and guaranteed. I've replaced such a ridiculous number of computer fans I would certainly know. So they put something in here that will actually last, and that you can depend on for a good long while, and not expect to hear it start screeching at you when you turn your computer on one day soon. But, like all things with moving parts, it WILL fail eventually, and because the front fan is special, it's pretty irreplaceable.

But, also, this DOES have an internal fan as well. And though they have a wire harness that connects them both (and to the motherboard and RGB header at the other end) which is proprietary for the 2 fans, you CAN use this cooler with only 1 fan on the inside if you like. And the fan on the inside is a normal 120mm fan, so if it goes bad, you CAN replace that fan with any old fan of your choosing. So, even if the "Koala fan" special fan on the front goes bad eventually, this will still be a perfectly functioning CPU cooler.

So, I took -1 star for the special fan on the front that is otherwise irreplaceable, but please realize that this definitely shouldn't turn you away from this CPU cooler. With double ball bearing fans, you should expect a very good life span from the fans to begin with, and you can always use it with the "hidden" fan inside.

Had they have built a cage to encompass a REGULAR 120mm fan on the front, rather than engineering a special fan with built-in brackets, I would have given this 5 stars all the way. In fact, if Amazon would let me, I'd really rate this 4.5 stars, instead of 4. Because the fan issue really is a very minor issue, it's just one that I felt was worthy of attention. This is, by matter of fact, a fantastic CPU cooler. As someone who has paid 2x this for CPU coolers, I find the asking price for something of this...fantastic quality...to be very reasonable. Also, as a side note, the packaging this comes in is just beautiful. 100% giftable to the "computer geek" in your life, the packaging could be on the shelf of any store, and it would be catching eyes doing so.

In all, I am VERY impressed with this cpu cooler, and I can hardly wait to get it installed on my i7 13700k and start recording some temps. I'm probably about a month away from getting that system together, but once I do, I'll update this with some real-world test results. Until then, this is a solid CPU cooler with some of the best machine work and build quality that I've seen. If you're building an air-cooled rig, this cooler should be very high on your short list.
